subject: API deprecation: /v1/batch-export endpoint – migration notes
body_text:
Team,

As a reminder, the /v1/batch-export endpoint will return 410 Gone on January 15. If you're still calling it, here's the minimal migration:

  # Old (deprecated)
  curl -X POST https://api.enterprise.local/v1/batch-export \
       -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
       -d '{"table": "events", "format": "csv"}'

  # New (v2)
  curl -X POST https://api.enterprise.local/v2/exports \
       -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
       -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
       -d '{"source": "events", "format": "csv", "async": true}'

The v2 endpoint returns a job ID immediately; poll /v2/exports/{id} for completion. Rate limits are also raised from 5 to 25 req/min.

If you hit any issues during cutover, file under ticket PLAT-7801 and tag #migration-v2.

Rafael
Platform Engineering

subject: Strategy summary: Analytics & Intelligence – FY25 operating plan
body_text:
Team,

Ahead of the Monday leadership sync, here's a condensed summary of where we're heading in FY25. Full deck to follow; this is the one-page version.

North Star: Reduce time-to-insight from 48h to under 6h for 80% of standard queries.

Three bets:
1. Self-serve data mesh – let product squads own their own domain models. Target: 12 domains live by Q2.
2. LLM-assisted query layer – "Project Oracle" pilot with the support-analytics use case. Budget approved; see ticket ANLY-2204 for the capex line.
3. Real-time event streaming – replace the nightly batch jobs with a Kafka-backed pipeline. Infra team has committed to the migration window in Jan-Feb.

Team structure: we're absorbing the 4 FTEs from the legacy reporting group. I'll send individual 1:1 invites this week.

Questions? Ping me directly. Let's make FY25 the year analytics stops being a bottleneck.

Kevin
Head of Analytics & Intelligence

subject: [enterprise/api-gateway] PR #1204 merged: Rate-limit header propagation fix
body_text:
sarah.kim merged pull request #1204 in enterprise/api-gateway

Title:  Fix rate-limit header propagation on upstream 502 responses
Branch: fix/ratelimit-502 → main
Commit: 9f3a2c1d8e4b

Changes: 4 files changed, 67 insertions(+), 12 deletions(-)
  - middleware/ratelimit.go
  - middleware/ratelimit_test.go
  - proxy/upstream.go
  - docs/CHANGELOG.md

The fix ensures that X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset headers are forwarded even when the upstream returns a 502 Gateway Timeout. Previously the headers were dropped in the error path, causing downstream clients to misinterpret the throttle window.

Reviewed by: j.park, t.nguyen

P.S. Nice catch on the test matrix, @sarah.kim — the 502-with-empty-body case is now covered.

View this pull request: https://github.com/enterprise/api-gateway/pull/1204

— GitHub Notifications

subject: [enterprise/checkout-service] Issue #891 assigned to you: Pagination cursor drift on /v2/orders
body_text:
j.park assigned this issue to t.nguyen.

Issue #891: Pagination cursor drift on /v2/orders
Label:  api, bug, P2
Milestone: v3.29.0

Description (by j.park):
  When a client pages through /v2/orders with limit=50, the cursor
  returned on page N does not always correspond to the correct offset
  if any order in the window is soft-deleted between page fetches.
  Result: the client sees either a duplicate or a skipped order.

  Repro:
    # page 1
    curl -s https://api.enterprise.local/v2/orders?limit=2&cursor= \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" | jq '.orders[].id'

    # delete one order in the window via admin API
    curl -X DELETE https://api.enterprise.local/v2/orders/ORD-99821 \
      -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>"

    # page 2 – one order is missing
    curl -s https://api.enterprise.local/v2/orders?limit=2&cursor=eyJvcmRlcklkIjoxMDAsInRzIjoxNzE…
      -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" | jq '.orders[].id'

  Suggested fix: use a composite (created_at, order_id) cursor instead
  of a bare offset, and validate cursor integrity server-side.

  Related: PROJ-4812 (Jira)

  (In-Reply-To: issue #887 "cursor pagination RFC" – this is the
   implementation defect that RFC #887 identified as a known gap.)

— GitHub Notifications

To unsubscribe: https://github.com/enterprise/checkout-service/issues/891#unsubscribe

subject: [JIRA] New issue assigned to you: PROJ-4821 – Fix null pointer in payment gateway retry logic
body_text:
Hi Maria,

A new issue has been created and assigned to you.

Issue: PROJ-4821
Summary: Fix null pointer in payment gateway retry logic
Priority: High
Sprint: Sprint 14 – Phoenix Q3
Reported by: dev.chen@enterprise.local

Description:
The retry handler in PaymentGatewayClient.java throws a NullPointerException when the upstream service returns a 204 with an empty body. The following snippet reproduces the issue locally:

    Response resp = httpClient.send(request, BodyHandlers.ofString());
    if (resp.statusCode() == 204) {
        JsonNode payload = mapper.readTree(resp.body()); // NPE here
        scheduleRetry(payload.get("txn_id"));
    }

Following up on ticket CS-2025-3312 (Severity: P2).

Root cause: A misconfigured circuit-breaker threshold in our service-mesh gateway (Ironclad v3.2, deployed 03-Jun) was capping per-tenant throughput well below your entitled quota. The fix was deployed at 21:42 UTC and all tenants in your region have been verified at full quota.

Action taken:
  1. Rolled back the offending mesh policy.
  2. Re-validated Fabrikam's /v2/ingest throughput (sustained 10,005 req/min over 5 min).
  3. Filed internal ticket INFRA-2025-0981 to add regression tests to the Ironclad release pipeline.

We sincerely apologise for the disruption to your ETL schedule. If you experience any further throttling before your 06:00 UTC window, reply to this thread and we will prioritise immediately.

Best regards,
Support Lead, Enterprise Platforms

subject: [Action Required] 2025 Security Policy Update – Mandatory Acknowledgment by Aug 1
body_text:
Dear All,

The Office of the CISO has published the 2025 revision of the Enterprise Security Policy (document ref: SEC-POL-2025-001). This revision consolidates several previously separate bulletins into a single governing document and introduces updated requirements in the following areas:

  1. Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
  2. Endpoint Encryption Standards
  3. Third-Party Vendor Access Controls
  4. Incident Reporting Timelines

Key changes you should note:
- MFA is now mandatory for ALL systems, including internal wikis, CI/CD pipelines, and shared infrastructure consoles. Phishing-resistant methods (FIDO2/WebAuthn) are preferred; TOTP remains acceptable through Q1 2026.
- Endpoint encryption must use AES-256 or equivalent. Legacy AES-128 configurations must be migrated by 2025-09-30.
- Vendor access tokens must have a maximum validity of 72 hours and must be stored in the enterprise vault (VaultCluster-03).
- Security incidents must be reported to sec-ops@enterprise.local within 4 hours of discovery. Previously this was 24 hours.

Full policy text and the change log are available at:
https://wiki.enterprise.local/policies/security/SEC-POL-2025-001

You are required to acknowledge receipt and comprehension of this policy via the LMS portal (Learning Management System → Compliance → 2025 Security Policy Acknowledgment) no later than Friday, August 1, 2025, 17:00 UTC.

Failure to complete the acknowledgment may result in restricted system access per the Access Management Addendum (AMA-2024).

If you have questions or believe a specific requirement conflicts with your team's operational workflow, please raise a ticket in the SEC-OPS queue (category: Policy-Feedback) before the deadline. Do NOT send credentials or key material via email.

Regards,
Office of the Chief Information Security Officer

subject: RE: Data Retention Policy v3.2 – Implementation Timeline & Config Changes
body_text:
Hi team,

Following up on last week's thread, Legal has finalized Data Retention Policy v3.2 (DRP-3.2). The effective date is 2025-10-01, and the migration window for your pipelines is 6 weeks.

The critical change for the data-engineering group is the new classification-to-retention mapping. Your existing YAML manifests in the retention-config repo will need updating. Here is the target structure:

  retention_policy:
    version: "3.2"
    scope: "prod-pipelines"
    classes:
      - name: customer_pii
        retain_days: 365
        then_action: pseudonymize
      - name: transactional_logs
        retain_days: 180
        then_action: archive_cold
      - name: debug_traces
        retain_days: 30
        then_action: purge
    override:
      legal_hold: true
      jurisdiction: [EU, US-CA]

Note: the "then_action" field replaces the old "lifecycle_end" key. Any pipelines still referencing the old key will fail validation in the next release of the retention-validator CLI.

Also a reminder: if your team processes any data originating from the EU or California, the 365-day ceiling for customer_pii is absolute. There is no waiver process. If you need to retain longer for a specific research project, you must file a Data Processing Impact Assessment (DPIA) with the DPO office at least 90 days before the new deadline.

Open question for the group: does the analytics team's batch job (job_id: ANL-BATCH-4471) fall under transactional_logs or customer_pii? The legal team needs a definitive answer by July 20 to lock the classification matrix.

Please confirm receipt and flag any pipeline that will be affected.

Thanks,
Priya Raman

body_text:
All Team Members,

As part of our annual compliance cycle, every employee, contractor, and intern at enterprise.local must complete the Code of Conduct Refresher module (module ID: COC-2025-ANNUAL).

  Platform: LMS → Compliance → COC-2025-ANNUAL

A few clarifications that the HR team has received questions about:

Q: Does the conflict-of-interest section apply if a family member is employed by a vendor we do NOT currently do business with?

A: You may, provided you do not disclose non-public information, project codenames, or internal metrics. The key test is: _would a reasonable person believe you are speaking as an official representative?_ If yes, you need to follow the Communications approval workflow.

Q: What counts as "confidential information" under the updated NDA scope?
A: Effectively anything tagged CONFIDENTIAL or RESTRICTED in our document classification scheme (see DCS-2024). This now explicitly includes sprint backlogs, unreleased feature names, and customer contract terms.

Non-completion will be reported to your direct manager on July 16. Persistent non-completion (beyond 14 days past deadline) may be treated as a policy violation under COC §7.4.

subject: FW: New MFA Enforcement – Service Accounts (Policy SEC-2025-014)
body_text:
Hi dev team,

Forwarding the policy update from the CISO office (see below). The action items specific to the dev-team are as follows:

Starting 2025-08-15, all service accounts used in CI/CD, IaC, and deployment pipelines MUST have MFA enforced. This includes machine-to-machine tokens. The technical implementation is a two-factor check at the API gateway layer.

Here is the expected configuration for your pipeline manifests (Terraform example):

  resource "service_account_policy" "ci_deploy" {
    name           = "svc_ci_deploy"
    project        = "prod-pipelines"
    mfa_required   = true
    mfa_provider   = "fido2-vault"
    token_ttl_sec  = 259200   # 72 hours max
    rotation       = "auto"
    rotation_days  = 7
  }

If your current pipeline uses a long-lived static token, you will need to migrate to the vault-issued ephemeral token flow. The migration guide is in the wiki: https://wiki.enterprise.local/eng/mfa-service-accounts

Timeline:
  - July 1: policy takes effect (read-only enforcement, warnings logged)
  - Aug 15: hard enforcement begins (requests without MFA token will be rejected with HTTP 401)
  - Sep 1: legacy token endpoints decommissioned

If your team's pipeline will be impacted, please open a ticket in the SEC-OPS queue with tag [MFA-MIGRATION] by end of June so we can schedule a migration window.

Do not post token values, vault paths, or credential material in tickets or chat channels.

Thanks,
IT Security Engineering

subject: Code of Conduct – Remote Work Guidelines (Rev. 4.1) Now in Effect
body_text:
Team,

Effective immediately, Revision 4.1 of the Remote Work Guidelines (a supplement to the Code of Conduct) is in effect. This revision was prompted by feedback from the Q1 employee survey and a review by the People & Culture legal team.

Key updates in Rev. 4.1:

1. Workspace Security
   Your home or co-working workspace must meet the same physical-security baseline as an enterprise office. Specifically:
   - No shared/public terminals for enterprise work
   - Screen-lock within 60 seconds of inactivity (this is enforced by the MDM profile; if it is not, file a ticket with it-mdm@enterprise.local)
   - Document storage: no physical printed copies of RESTRICTED or CONFIDENTIAL material in home offices without a locked cabinet (standard: EN 1040-1 or equivalent)

2. Communication & Availability
   - Your stated working hours (in the team calendar) define your availability window. Outside that window, you are not expected to respond to non-urgent messages.
   - The "right to disconnect" clause (COC §12.3) applies equally to remote and office-based staff. Managers must respect it.
   - Video-on is encouraged for 1:1s and team syncs but is not mandated. _Is video required for client-facing calls?_ Yes, per the Client Interaction Standard (CIS-2024), video must be on unless the client explicitly prefers otherwise.

3. Data Handling at Home
   - Enterprise data must not be transferred to personal devices, personal cloud storage, or personal email.
   - Screenshots of enterprise applications are prohibited unless the app is explicitly marked "shareable."
   - If you work in a co-working space, you must use the enterprise VPN and must NOT use the co-working space's local Wi-Fi for any enterprise traffic. The MDM profile will enforce this, but please be aware that a = violation of this rule is treated as a data-security incident, not a policy infraction. The distinction matters for reporting.

4. Well-being & Boundary Expectations
   - Rev. 4.1 adds explicit language: an employee's choice to log off and not respond outside working hours is a protected right. Retaliation for exercising this right is a Code of Conduct violation under §9 (Harassment & Retaliation).

Full text: https://wiki.enterprise.local/hr/policies/remote-work-rev4-1

Acknowledgment is collected via the LMS. Deadline: July 31.

If you have a question about how a specific rule applies to your setup, your People Partner is the right contact. Do not guess.

Best,
People & Culture
enterprise.local

subject: Acceptable Use Policy – 2025 Revision (AUP-2025) Published
body_text:
All Employees, Contractors, and Temporary Staff,

The Acceptable Use Policy (AUP-2025) has been published and is effective 2025-07-01. This document governs the use of all enterprise computing resources, including:

  - Corporate laptops, desktops, and mobile devices
  - Enterprise network (wired, Wi-Fi, VPN)
  - SaaS applications (email, collaboration, cloud IDEs, CI/CD)
  - Shared infrastructure (k8s clusters, object storage, data warehouses)
  - Internal wiki, LMS, and ticketing systems

What changed from AUP-2023:

  Section 4.2 – Personal Software
    Previously: "Personal software may be installed if it does not conflict with approved tooling."
    Now: Personal software installation is prohibited on managed endpoints. Use the sanctioned app catalog (see https://wiki.enterprise.local/it/app-catalog). If you need a tool that is not in the catalog, submit an App-Request ticket. The IT Security team will assess within 10 business days.

  Section 6.1 – AI & Generative Tools
    A new section. Summary:
    - You may use AI-assisted coding tools (Copilot, etc.) for drafting.
    - You MUST NOT paste CONFIDENTIAL or RESTRICTED source code, customer data, or internal architecture diagrams into any public or third-party AI service.
    - Enterprise-deployed AI instances (the on-prem LLM gateway) are approved for all internal workloads.
    - Output from any AI tool is your responsibility to review. You are the author of record.

  Section 8.3 – Shadow IT
    "Shadow IT" is defined as any system, service, or pipeline that processes enterprise data or enterprise credentials without a record in the Service Catalog (cat_id format: SVC-YYYY-NNNN). If you discover a shadow-IT system, report it to it-security@enterprise.local. Do not attempt to decommission it yourself.

  Section 11 – Incident Reporting
    Reporting window reduced from 24 hours to 4 hours (aligned with SEC-POL-2025-001 §9). Report to sec-ops@enterprise.local. Include: what happened, when, which systems were affected, and your best-guess data classification of anything involved. You do NOT need to have a full root-cause analysis before reporting.

  Section 14 – Termination of Access
    Access revocation is same-day upon separation. The IT Provisioning team will execute. You will receive a 48-hour window to retrieve personal files from your mailbox and home directory. After that, all data is purged per DRP-3.2.

The full policy, including all appendices and the glossary, is at:
https://wiki.enterprise.local/policies/aup/AUP-2025

Acknowledgment is required in the LMS by July 31, 2025.

This policy is a living document. Amendments will be published in the same wiki location with a changelog. You will receive an email notification for any material change.

Compliance with the AUP is a condition of continued access to enterprise systems. Violations are addressed through the disciplinary framework in the Code of Conduct (§5 – Misconduct; §7 – Policy Violations).

Regards,
Office of the CISO
enterprise.local

subject: [EXTERNAL] TK-45387 – Summary of investigation & next steps (Severity: P2)
body_text:
Dear Mr. Tanaka,

Thank you for your patience while we investigated the intermittent 503 errors you experienced between 09:42 and 11:15 UTC on the /v2/webhooks/ingest endpoint.

Root Cause:
Our edge-load-balancer cluster (eu-west-2, zone c) experienced a certificate-rotation failure. The intermediate CA bundle was stale, causing TLS handshakes to time out for approximately 93 minutes. This was a configuration drift introduced by an automated cert-manager job.

Impact:
- 47 webhook deliveries delayed or dropped (all retried successfully by 11:20 UTC)
- No data loss confirmed
- SLA credit of 2.5% will be applied to your next invoice

Preventive Actions:
1. Cert-manager rotation window has been moved to the maintenance window (Sun 02:00–04:00 UTC)
2. A synthetic probe now alerts the on-call if handshake latency exceeds 800 ms
3. Redundant CA bundle pinning added to zone-c LB config

If you require a formal incident report for your internal records, reply to this email and we will generate it under NDA reference FAB-ENT-2025.

Kind regards,
R. Okafor
Senior Support Engineer, Tier-2
Enterprise Support – Platform Team

subject: ESCALATION: TK-45198 – Fabrikam production outage, 4,200 users impacted, SEV-1
body_text:
Team,

Escalating this from Tier-2 to the incident channel. Full context below.

SUMMARY
Customer: Fabrikam GmbH (tenant: fabrikam-prod)
Ticket: TK-45198 | Severity: SEV-1 (customer-side P1: FAB-OPS-2025-0003)
Window: 06:12 – 07:48 UTC (ongoing at time of writing)
Impact: 4,200 concurrent sessions dropped; web portal and mobile API both returning 502 from the gateway tier.

TIMELINE
06:12 – First PagerDuty alert (5xx spike on api-fabrikam-prod-01)
06:18 – On-call (L. Okafor) confirms all 3 API pods in eu-west-2a are crash-looping
06:24 – Suspected bad deploy of config-service v2.14.1 (rolled out 05:58 UTC as part of nightly batch)
06:31 – Rollback initiated; pods remain unhealthy after 6 min
06:47 – Root cause identified: v2.14.1 introduced a null-ref in the feature-flag resolver when a tenant's flag schema has fewer than 3 keys. Fabrikam's schema has exactly 2 keys ("beta" and "canary").
06:55 – Hotfix v2.14.2 deployed to staging; passing smoke tests
07:12 – Hotfix promoted to eu-west-2a; 2 of 3 pods recovered
07:30 – Remaining pod recovered; error rates back to baseline (<0.1%)
07:48 – All 4,200 sessions re-established; customer confirmed recovery via phone bridge

AFFECTED CUSTOMER FACING ITEMS
- Web dashboard: 502 for 96 min
- Mobile SDK v4.x: connection refused, forced offline mode
- Webhook delivery: 1,832 events queued and replayed (no loss)
- SSO: unaffected (separate infra)

CREDS / VULT NOTE
During the incident, the on-call engineer needed to access the tenant's vault-managed signing keys to verify webhook replay signatures. Access was granted via the break-glass procedure (BK-2025-0189) and logged. No key material was exported or logged in plaintext. The keys remain encrypted in HSM.

NEXT STEPS
1. Post-incident review scheduled Thu 14:00 UTC (invite in #inc-45198)
2. Customer to receive formal RCA within 5 business days per SLA §7.2
3. Feature-flag resolver to be gated: minimum 3-key schema enforced at deploy-time with a CI check (ticket ENG-7742)
4. PagerDuty escalation policy updated – SEV-1 auto-pages support-lead + CTO office after 15 min

Customer POC: Anna Müller (IT Security Eng) and Dr. Stefan Meyer (Procurement). Both on the bridge.

Please do NOT reply-all. Use the incident channel.

– W. Chen
Support Engineering Manager, Platform
enterprise.local | TK-45198 | SEV-1 (resolving)

subject: UPDATED: Invoice Processing & AP Guidelines Effective 2024-12-01
body_text:
All staff,

Effective December 1, 2024, the following changes to our invoice processing and accounts-payable guidelines take effect. These updates were approved by the Finance Committee on 2024-10-22 and are being communicated under policy ref FIN-POL-2024-007.

1. PO Threshold Raise
   Purchase orders are now required for any single vendor transaction exceeding $1,500 (previously $1,000). Transactions at or below $1,500 may be processed via the corporate card with a receipt attached in the expense portal within 5 business days.

2. Three-Way Match Enforcement
   All invoices must match the PO number, the receiving report (goods receipt), and the invoice line items before payment release. Invoices failing the three-way match will be placed on a 10-business-day hold. Repeated failures (3+ in a quarter) will trigger a vendor review by Procurement.

3. Expense Report Turnaround
   Employee expense reports must be submitted within 10 calendar days of the expense (previously 15). Approval must occur within 5 business days of submission. Reports older than 30 days will be auto-rejected and require re-submission with a written justification memo to your department head.

4. Vendor Onboarding
   New vendors must complete the W-9 / W-8BEN collection and the security questionnaire (SEC-VQ-3) before their first invoice is accepted. AP will reject invoices from vendors not present in the vendor master.

5. Dispute SLA
   Disputed invoices must be logged in the AP portal within 5 business days of receipt. The vendor will be contacted within 2 business days of the dispute being logged. Resolution target: 15 business days.

Effective date: Monday, 2024-12-01.
Questions: ap-helpdesk@enterprise.local or #ap-policies in Teams.

Thank you for your compliance.

subject: ⚠ Phishing Drill Results – Q2 2025 (click rate: 12.4%)
body_text:
Hello everyone,

Our quarterly phishing simulation (run 27 May, 09:00 UTC) is now complete. I want to share the results and, more importantly, what to do if you see something suspicious.

Headline numbers (org-wide, n = 4,217):
  - Clicked the lure link: 12.4% (Q1: 15.1% – improvement)
  - Clicked AND submitted fake credentials: 3.8%
  - Reported via the "Report Phish" button: 8.7%

The Q2 lure mimicked an "invoice payment failed" email from litwareinc.com with a link to a lookalike domain. If you clicked it, no real data was transmitted – the page was a harmless tracking form. However, if you entered your corporate password on that page, rotate it immediately at https://sso.enterprise.local/change-pw and contact the Help Desk.

What to look for:
  1. Sender domain doesn't match the display name
  2. Urgency language ("act within 24 hours", "your account will be suspended")
  3. Shortened or lookalike URLs (litswareinc.com vs litwareinc.com)
  4. Attachments with double extensions (.pdf.exe, .docm.zip)

Reporting: hover over the subject line in Outlook → "Report Phish". This tags the message for the SOC team and removes it from your inbox.

Full report and training modules: https://security.enterprise.local/phishing-q2

Stay sharp out there.

– Raj & the SOC Team

subject: Post-Mortem: 19 May 03:12–04:47 UTC – DC-07 / DC-08 replication storm (INC-4472)
body_text:
To all affected engineering and platform teams,

Below is the post-mortem for the Active Directory replication storm that impacted build pipelines and SSO from 03:12 to 04:47 UTC on 19 May.

TL;DR: A misconfigured DFSR interval on DC-07 triggered a cascading sync across 14 domain controllers, saturating the 10 Gb uplink and causing 95 s average auth latency for ~95 minutes.

Timeline (UTC):
  03:12  DFSR replication cycle begins on DC-07 with interval set to 60 s (should be 3600 s)
  03:14  DC-08 inherits the aggressive interval via FSMO metadata
  03:19  10 Gb uplink to the core switch hits 97% utilization
  03:22  SSO portal p99 latency crosses 8 s; PagerDuty fires for SLO breach
  03:31  On-call (D. Okafor) identifies DFSR as root cause via `dcdiag /v`
  03:44  DFSR interval reset to 3600 s on all 14 DCs; sync backlog begins draining
  04:10  Uplink utilization back below 40%
  04:47  SSO p99 back under 800 ms; all alerts resolved

Root cause: A change (CHG-2025-1183) deployed the previous night set the DFSR interval via a GPO that lacked a scope filter. The filter was intended to exclude DC-07 and DC-08 (the FSMO holders) but the OU path had a trailing-underscore typo (OU_DC_FSMO vs OU_DC-FSMO).

Impact:  ~340 CI jobs retried; 0 data loss; 0 user data exposed.

Corrective actions (ticket INC-4472-CA):
  1. [DONE] Fix GPO scope filter; add regression test to the DC change pipeline
  2. [DONE] Add a canary check that alerts if DFSR interval < 300 s on any DC
  3. [DUE 30 Jun] Implement a change-freeze window for FSMO holder GPOs (ticket CHG-PROC-044)
  4. [DUE 15 Jul] Rate-limit replication storms at the switch level via CoS markings

Lessons learned: A single-character typo in an OU path had org-wide blast radius. We will require peer review + a 24-hour bake period for any GPO touching the FSMO holder OU starting next sprint.

Full report with packet captures and GPO diff: https://wiki.enterprise.local/postmortems/INC-4472

Thank you for your patience during the incident. If your team has follow-up questions, reply to this thread or raise a ticket referencing INC-4472.

Best regards,
Dana Okafor
Site Reliability Engineering – On-call Lead
enterprise.local

subject: FW: MFA Phase 2 – service account exceptions and CI/CD impact (SEC-2291)
body_text:
Hi Eng team,

Following up on the MFA Phase 2 enrolment email, a few specifics for the engineering org:

Q: Do CI/CD runners (GitHub Actions self-hosted, Jenkins agents) need MFA?
A: No. Service accounts authenticated via client-secret or mTLS certs are excluded. The exclusion is registered under the "svc_ci" SPN group. Do NOT add human accounts to that group – it's a hard block on the IdP side.

Q: What about the local `git config credential.helper` stored token?
A: The stored token remains valid. However, if you use a personal PAT for any manual push, that PAT will now require a TOTP code at each use after 1 July. I'd recommend migrating to a fine-grained app-specific token before then. Docs: https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens

Q: I'm on the on-call rotation and need 24/7 access. Will I be locked out if my phone dies?
A: The FIDO2 hardware key (YubiKey) works offline. Each on-call engineer gets a second key shipped to their desk this week. If both keys and your phone are unavailable, the IT Help Desk (ext. 5100) can issue a 6-hour one-time code after dual-manager verbal approval.

Q: The TOTP code window – is it 30 s or 60 s?
A: 30 s standard, ±1 clock-drift step (so effectively 60 s). Make sure your phone's system clock is NTP-synced (`ntp date --server ntp.enterprise.local`).

Let me know if you have additional questions. We'll hold a 20-min Q&A on Thursday 14:00 in Room 4B / Zoom.

Cheers,
Tomás
Platform Engineering – Identity & Access

subject: 30-second phishing refresher – the "invoice from litwareinc.com" pattern
body_text:
Heads-up: we've seen a 4× spike in "payment failed / invoice overdue" lures targeting the AP team and, increasingly, non-finance staff.

The pattern:
  1. Sender: ap-billing@litwareinc.com (or a near-miss like litwareinc-billing.com)
  2. Subject: "ACTION REQUIRED – Invoice #48291 overdue"
  3. Body: urgent tone, 24-hr deadline, link to "resolve" the payment
  4. The link goes to a domain like litwareinc-invoice[.]xyz (note the brackets – that's how we write it in reports; the actual email shows a clean URL)

Three things to check before clicking ANY link in a finance-related email:
  • Hover the link. Does the domain match litwareinc.com exactly?
  • Does the sender's full address appear in the To/Cc, or only in the body?
  • Do you actually have an outstanding invoice with that vendor? Check the AP portal, don't guess.

If in doubt: don't click. Forward to security@enterprise.local or use Outlook → Report Phish.

No shame in asking – better a 2-minute verification than a 2-week incident.

– SOC Team

subject: Brief Outage Notice – SSO portal degraded 14:02–14:11 UTC today (INC-4508)
body_text:
Dear Colleagues,

Between 14:02 and 14:11 UTC today, the SSO portal experienced elevated latency (p99 ≈ 6 s) and a small number of failed login attempts. The issue was traced to a mis-applied connection-pool setting on the load-balancer pair (LB-SSO-01 / LB-SSO-02) following a routine config push.

The fix was rolled back within 4 minutes of detection. No user data was affected and no credentials were exposed. All sessions that were active during the window remain valid.

We apologise for the disruption and are adding a pre-push validation step to the LB config pipeline (ticket LB-3391) to prevent recurrence.

Full technical report: https://wiki.enterprise.local/incidents/INC-4508

If you experienced a failed login during that window and your credentials still work, no further action is needed. If you are still unable to authenticate, please contact the IT Help Desk (ext. 5100).

Thank you for your patience.

Kind regards,
Marcus Webb
IT Operations Lead

subject: Deprecating legacy API keys - migration timeline (Epic-2049)
body_text:
Engineering team,

I wanted to give everyone a heads-up on the timeline we've locked in for the legacy API key deprecation under Epic-2049. This is the migration you've been asking about for a few sprints now, and I know it touches a lot of surfaces, so I'll walk through the phases.

Phase 1 (now through 21 June): We are entering dual-read mode. The old v1 keys will still be accepted by the gateway, but every request authenticated with a v1 key will emit a deprecation warning header and a structured log entry. No functional change yet—this is purely so we can measure how much traffic is still riding on the old format. The log entries go to our observability stack, not to any email list, so if your service is still using a v1 key you will only see it in the APM dashboards.

Phase 2 (22 June – 5 July): The gateway will start rate-limiting v1-key requests to 10 req/s. This is deliberately below the production load for most services, so if you notice a 429 spike around that window, check whether your integration is still presenting a v1-format key and switch it to the v2 token pulled from the vault. The vault path for v2 tokens is /prod/api-gateway/v2-tokens/<service-name>. If your service doesn't have an entry there yet, open a ticket with the platform team and we'll cut one.

Phase 3 (6 July onward): v1 keys are hard-rejected. Any request presenting a v1-format key will receive a 401 with a machine-readable error code. We will not be maintaining a compatibility shim past this date. If a downstream partner (including Fabrikam's sandbox) is still on v1, their team has been notified separately and has until the 30th of June to migrate.

A few practical notes for those of you who are still on v1:

First, the v1 keys are stored in the old flat-file format under /legacy/tokens/ in the vault. We are NOT going to migrate those files automatically. You need to generate a fresh v2 token, register it under the new path, update your service's bootstrap code to call the vault agent, and then we'll decommission the flat file. Do not copy the v1 value into a v2 field—the validation will reject it and you'll just waste a support ticket.

Second, I understand some of you have the v1 key baked into a Helm chart value or a Terraform variable from 2022. If that's the case, please flag it in Epic-2049 so we can coordinate a chart update. We do not want to surprise anyone during the cutover window.

Third, and this is important: none of this changes the password or credential that your service account uses to authenticate to the vault itself. The vault login credential and the API token it dispenses are separate things. Rotating one does not affect the other. If you are unsure which is which, the LMS module I mentioned in last week's training email covers the distinction.

If you have questions, the best place is the #api-gateway-migration channel. I will be in there most days this week. For anything that might become an incident, use the SRE on-call rota rather than pinging me directly.

Thanks for your patience through this. It's a big migration but it will make the next two years of API governance a lot less painful.

— Paloma
Platform Architecture
enterprise.local

subject: Reminder: Use the enterprise password manager for service accounts
body_text:
Hi all,

Quick reminder from the IT helpdesk: if your team maintains any service-account credentials (database passwords, API tokens, webhook secrets, SFTP keys), please store them in the enterprise password manager and reference them by vault path in your code and configs.

We are still seeing a small number of cases where credentials end up in:
  - personal notes apps or sticky notes under a monitor
  - shared Excel or CSV files in the team drive
  - Slack or Teams DMs
  - local .env files on a laptop

None of these are acceptable under SEC-POL-007. The password manager supports MFA, audit logging, and per-person access control, so there is no operational reason to keep a secret anywhere else.

If you are in a bind and cannot access the vault (e.g., you are on a road trip and the vault endpoint is unreachable), the break-glass procedure is documented in the IT Service Desk knowledge base under "Emergency credential access." Do NOT improvise a workaround.

If you find a credential that was shared in one of the informal channels above, treat it as compromised and rotate it immediately. Open a ticket so we can track the incident.

Thanks for keeping our environment safe.

— IT Helpdesk

subject: RE: FW: Open Enrollment FAQ – Top 10 Questions (Updated Jul 14)
body_text:
Hi everyone,

Following up on the thread from last week, here's the consolidated FAQ. We've added three new questions based on the volume of tickets we've seen (HR-2025-0487 through HR-2025-0512).

1. Can I change my election after the Jul 30 deadline?
   Only for qualifying life events (marriage, birth, loss of other coverage). Otherwise, changes wait until next cycle.

2. I'm a new hire starting in August. Do I need to enroll?
   Yes. New-hire enrollment window is your start date + 30 days. Use the same portal; select "New Hire" on the welcome screen.

3. What happens to my FSA balance if I stop contributing?
   Unspent funds are forfeited at plan-year end unless you elected the carryover option (up to $640).

4. Can I add a domestic partner?
   Under our current carrier rules, no. We are reviewing this with Legal for the 2026 cycle (ticket HR-2025-0512).

5. Is the new telehealth benefit covered for prescriptions?
   Telehealth visits: yes, $0 copay. Prescriptions filled via mail-order pharmacy: standard formulary applies.

6. My spouse's employer plan is cheaper. Can I waive our plan?
   Yes, via the waiver form in the portal (Benefits → Waivers). Keep a copy for your records.

7. Do the wellness-program sessions count as PTO?
   No. They are during lunch hours and are optional.

8. Can I split my HSA contribution between individual and family tiers?
   No—your tier is determined by your coverage election. The contribution limit is all-or-nothing per tier.

9. What's the process if I disagree with a carrier's prior-auth denial?
   File an internal appeal within 180 days. HR Benefits (ext. 5102) will help you assemble the packet. Average resolution: 22 business days.

10. Is there a penalty for late new-hire enrollment?
    You'll pay the full premium out of pocket for the gap period. We recommend enrolling on day one.

Full policy PDF and plan documents are in the HR Self-Service portal under Benefits → Documents.

Thanks,
HR Helpdesk
helpdesk@enterprise.local | ext. 5100

subject: Nimbus Platform Q3 Product Update – What's New & What's Coming

Feedback: nimbus-feedback@enterprise.local

Cheers,
The Nimbus Product Team

subject: Engineering Digest: Why _lazy_loading_ = performance wins?
body_text:
Subject of this week's digest: lazy loading and why it's the cheapest perf win in most SPAs.

Quick benchmarks we ran on the atlas_frontend repo (v3.12):

  - Initial bundle: 2.4 MB (without _lazy_loading_)
  - With route-level code splitting: 680 KB initial, rest deferred
  - LCP improvement: 1.2s → 0.6s on mid-tier mobile

Open question for the group: should we adopt the same pattern for the admin portal's _sidebar_components_? The trade-off = a slight complexity bump in the router config, but the TTI gain is measurable.

Slides & raw data: enterprise.local/wiki/perf/lazy-loading-benchmarks

Drop a comment or ping me on #perf-guild if you want to pair on a spike.

– Priya, Research Eng

subject: API Platform Update: v3 migration timeline & breaking changes
body_text:
Hi all,

A quick heads-up from the API Platform team. The v3 REST & GraphQL gateway goes GA on Dec 1. Here's what changes:

1. Auth: Bearer token header is now mandatory. The legacy X-Api-Key header = deprecated (removal in v4).
2. Rate limits: Default bucket shifts from 600 req/min → 200 req/min per tenant. Burst = 5x for 10s window.?
3. Pagination: cursor-based only. The old ?page=1&per_page=50 pattern will 400 after Dec 30.
4. Error envelope: standardized to { code, message, request_id, details: {} }. Existing parsers that expect _error_msg will break.
5. Webhooks: HMAC-SHA256 signature header (X-Signature_256) is now attached to every delivery.

Migration guide: enterprise.local/docs/api/v3-migration
Staging sandbox: available now – credentials provisioned via Vault (see #api-platform for the path).

Questions? Post in #api-platform or file a ticket with tag [v3-migration].

Thanks,
DevRel

subject: RE: Project Ledger – Treasury integration blockers
body_text:
Dear Treasury team,

Thank you for the detailed walkthrough on Tuesday. I want to confirm the three blockers we identified and assign owners before we lose the momentum:

1. SFTP key rotation cadence. Treasury requires 90-day rotation; our current pipeline assumes 180-day. Owner of the remediation: me. I will update the pipeline config and coordinate with the vault team for the key lifecycle change. Target: 14 Jul.

2. Settlement-file schema versioning. The Ledger spec (v2.3) expects a `settlement_ref` field that the Treasury gateway does not yet expose. Owner: Treasury side, J. Whitmore. I've logged it as LEDGER-4419. I'd appreciate a confirmed ETA by the end of this week so I can adjust the integration test matrix.

3. Idempotency key collision window. Our replay logic uses a 5-minute dedup window; Treasury's system uses 10 minutes. We need to align. I propose we adopt the 10-minute window across both systems. Owner: joint – me (Ledger) and J. Whitmore (Treasury) to confirm by Friday.

Risk to the overall Ledger timeline: if item 2 is not resolved by 01 Aug, the UAT window (08-12 Aug) will need to compress, which I do not recommend given the regulatory sign-off dependencies.

I will send a one-page summary to the Steering Committee on Monday. Please flag any objections by COB Thursday.

Regards,
Elena Petrov
Treasury Systems Integration, Enterprise
Ext. 4471

P.S. The key-rotation ticket (item 1) does NOT require any secrets to be shared over email or ticket systems. We will handle the actual key material through the HSM workflow only. Just clarifying for the audit trail.

Dear Operations Coordinator,

I am writing to provide an updated delivery schedule for PO#ENT-2025-3391, which covers the Q3 restock of consumer-facing product lines (families 2200-2299). I want to be upfront that we are experiencing some upstream delays with our resin supplier in the Guangdong region, and this is cascading into our production slots for the following weeks.

Here is the revised shipping plan:

Ship 4 (originally scheduled Jul 14): Now Jul 21. Contains 12,000 units of SKU 2241 (Puzzle Blocks, 100-pc) and 4,500 units of SKU 2258 (Marble Run, 48-pc). Consolidated into a single 40-ft container. ETA to your Rotterdam DC: Jul 29.

Ship 5 (originally scheduled Jul 28): Now Aug 04. Contains 8,000 units of SKU 2263 (Building Tiles, 60-pc) and 3,200 units of SKU 2270 (Nesting Cups, 12-pc). Two 20-ft containers. ETA to your Rotterdam DC: Aug 11.

Ship 6 (scheduled Aug 12): Unaffected. Contains 6,000 units of SKU 2285 (Stacking Rings, 8-pc). ETA Aug 19.

We understand your Q3 marketing push depends on Ship 4 landing before the Aug 1 retail reset window. To mitigate, we are expediting the final QA pass and will run a 48-hour overtime shift on the assembly line this weekend. That said, I cannot guarantee the Jul 21 date with 100% certainty; I will send a daily status update from Jul 18 onward until the container is at the port of Ningbo.

On the commercial side: no surcharge will be applied for the schedule shift. The late-delivery penalty clause in Section 18 of our MSA is waived for this instance as the root cause is a Tier-2 supplier issue outside our direct control. That said, we will credit 2% of the affected PO value if either Ship 4 or Ship 5 arrives more than 5 business days past the revised ETA.

Please confirm receipt of this schedule update by replying to this thread. If your DC team needs revised ASN numbers or updated BL references, let me know and I will have our freight forwarder (Maersk) issue amended documents within 24 hours.

Thank you for your patience. I know this is not the news you wanted to hear on a Monday morning.

subject: Contract Amendment Request – MSA #WT-2024-0847, Section 9 (Force Majeure)
body_text:
Dear Ms. Martinez,

As discussed on our call last Friday, we would like to propose a minor amendment to Section 9 (Force Majeure) of MSA #WT-2024-0847. Specifically, we are requesting that the notification window for force majeure events be extended from 5 to 10 business days, and that the list of qualifying events in Schedule C be updated to include "supply chain disruption at a Tier-2 or Tier-3 supplier outside the direct control of the notifying party."

This is a mutual provision – it would apply equally to your obligations under the agreement.

Rationale: as seen with the Q2 resin shortage, modern supply chains have 4-5 tiers of dependency, and a 5-day window is operationally unrealistic when the root cause is a Tier-3 chemical supplier in a different jurisdiction. The 10-day window is consistent with the terms in our MSAs with three other enterprise customers (happy to share anonymised excerpts if helpful).

Draft redline attached (Section 9, paragraphs 1 and 4; Schedule C, items 7-9). Total change: 6 lines of text.

We are happy to accept this as a stand-alone amendment or fold it into the renewal package we sent last week. Your preference?

Best,
Eleanor Fitch (cc'd for legal tracking)
Head of Commercial Legal, Wingtip Toys Ltd.
contracts@wingtiptoys.com

subject: RE: RE: Kubernetes node pool autoscaler stuck (INC-2025-0741)
body_text:
Patching the autoscaler config to set `min-replicas: 3` and restarting the cluster-autoscaler daemonset resolved the stuck state. The node pool in `prod-eu-west-1` is back to 12 nodes and draining correctly.

Root cause: a misconfigured `balance-similar-node-groups: false` flag combined with the new t5ad.2xlarge node type caused the autoscaler to refuse scale-up events because it couldn't find a "matching" group.

I've filed a ticket with our cloud provider to confirm the flag interaction is a known issue (their case #9981234).

Incident status: RESOLVED. Post-mortem doc will be in Confluence by COB tomorrow.

subject: RE: Code review – PR #2891 (feature: async export pipeline)
body_text:
Hi all,

I've pushed three commits addressing the review comments:

1. Replaced the blocking `export_to_csv()` call with an asyncio task that publishes progress events to the Redis pub/sub channel. This unblocks the event loop during large exports (>50k rows).
2. Added a `max_concurrent_exports` semaphore (default 4) to prevent resource exhaustion on the worker tier.
3. Moved the S3 pre-signed URL generation out of the request handler into a background task, as @sofia suggested.

Still open question: should we persist the export job ID in the user session or in a dedicated `export_jobs` table? Leaning toward the table for auditability, but want a second opinion from the data team before I commit to the schema.

On 2025-07-14, 15:33, Sofia Lindqvist <sofia.lindqvist@enterprise.local> wrote:
> Liam,
>
> Overall the design looks solid. Two things I'd push back on:
>
> 1. Generating the S3 pre-signed URL in the request handler means we're holding a connection for the duration of the URL generation + metadata fetch. For large exports this could be 2-3 seconds. Move it to the background task.
>
> 2. I don't see a concurrency cap. If ten users trigger exports simultaneously, we'll be hammering the S3 endpoint. Add a semaphore or use the existing `worker-pool` abstraction.
>
> Otherwise LGTM with those changes.
>
> – Sofia

subject: RE: [SEC-POL-2025-014] Password rotation policy update – feedback window
body_text:
Hi team,

The 30-day feedback window closes next Friday (2025-07-25). I wanted to highlight three points that I believe need clarification before we ratify:

1. **Service account credentials** – The draft says "all credentials must be rotated every 90 days." We need an explicit exclusion or separate policy for long-lived service accounts that can't be rotated without breaking integrations. Suggest a 365-day rotation with a 30-day advance warning ticket.

2. **Vault-managed secrets** – Since our HashiCorp Vault already handles automatic lease expiration, requiring manual 90-day rotation on top of Vault's lease is redundant and creates operational overhead. Propose: Vault-managed secrets are governed by their lease TTL, and the 90-day rule applies only to credentials stored outside Vault.

3. **Exception process** – The draft mentions an exception form but doesn't specify SLA for approval or the maximum exception duration. Suggest 14-day review SLA and a hard cap of 90 days for any exception.

I've drafted the language for all three points and attached as a redline. Happy to walk through on a call if easier.

>
> The proposed revision to the Corporate Password & Credential Rotation Policy is now open for a 30-day feedback period (2025-07-10 through 2025-07-25).
>
> Key changes in this revision:
> - Rotation interval reduced from 180 days to 90 days for all user and service credentials
> - Introduction of mandatory MFA step-up for any credential rotation action
> - New exception process with Security Governance approval
> - Clarification of scope: applies to all systems managed by Enterprise Local IT
>
> Please submit feedback via the policy portal or reply to this thread.
>
> – Security Governance Team

subject: API key rotation for payments-gateway – extended timeline and test plan
body_text:
Folks,

I wanted to walk through the plan for rotating the outbound API keys we use to call the payments-gateway microservice, since this one has a slightly longer blast radius than the usual quarterly rotation.

Background: we currently hold two active keys (primary + failover) that were issued back in the v2.1 migration. Both are scoped to read-only on the ledger endpoints but write on the settlement queue. The vendor (Adventure Works, their payments division) told us last month that their key-management backend is migrating to a new HSM cluster, and they recommend we re-issue from their side as well. So we're doing a dual rotation: we regenerate our client-side secrets AND they rotate their server-side validation keys. This means there's a window where we need both old and new to coexist.

Timeline (all UTC):
  Mon 09:00 – Announce freeze on any new key usage in #payments-alerts
  Mon 14:00 – Deploy new primary key to the canary pod (10% traffic)
  Mon 14:30 – Verify auth handshake in the integration test suite (suite ID: PG-IT-2024)
  Tue 06:00 – Shift 100% traffic to new primary
  Tue 06:30 – Confirm zero 401/403s in the last 30-min window
  Tue 18:00 – Revoke old primary
  Wed 09:00 – Rotate failover key (same canary → full → revoke pattern)
  Wed 17:00 – Close ticket PAY-3392 and archive the old key metadata in the vault audit log

What I need from each of you:
  1. Platform – confirm the Vault path /payments/prod/api-key-primary is writable by the deploy-bot and that the old entry will be tombstoned, not deleted, so we have an audit trail.
  2. SRE – set up the 401/403 alert threshold to fire at >5 requests/min during the window, and page me directly, not the on-call rotation.
  3. QA – the integration suite currently hardcodes a placeholder token. Please update it to read from the vault at runtime before Monday's canary. I know this is a 2-line change but I don't want to touch the test repo during a rotation window.
  4. Everyone – do NOT paste the new key values into Slack, JIRA comments, or PR descriptions. The vault is the only source of truth. If you need the value locally for a one-off curl test, use `vault read -field=value payments/prod/api-key-primary` and let it expire from your shell history.

If anything in this plan looks risky to you, flag it by end of day tomorrow. I'd rather adjust the schedule now than debug a settlement outage at 2 a.m.

Also – and I mean this kindly – I know last quarter's rotation was a scramble because we found out about the vendor's HSM migration only 48 hours out. This time we have three weeks. Let's actually use the time.

Thanks all,
Sofia

Sofia Feld
Senior Platform Engineer, Payments Infrastructure
enterprise.local | ext. 4417

"The best time to rotate a key is when nobody is looking. The second-best time is when you have a test plan."

subject: RE: Kepler Phase 2 – vault access request & credential inventory
body_text:
Hi Kepler team,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the access request. A few things I need to clarify before I approve the vault policy update:

1. You asked for read access to /kepler/prod/db-connection-string. That path currently holds a DSN that embeds the username and password for the analytics Postgres instance. I'm comfortable granting read, but I need to add a condition that the secret is only decryptable by roles tagged `kepler-phase2` AND that the TTL on the decrypted value is 15 minutes. Can you confirm your app's connection pooler supports short-lived credentials? I don't want to go to a 24-hour token just because the pooler expects a static string.

2. You also listed the S3 presigned-URL bucket key in your request. That one I'm going to decline and redirect. Presigned URLs should be generated at runtime by the gateway service; the raw bucket credential should never be exposed to the application tier. If you need S3 access, I'll add a scoped IAM role instead. Can you file that as a separate ticket under INFRA-XXXX so it gets its own review?

3. Minor thing – your PR to the kepler-config repo (PR #217) has a comment that says "password is in the vault, ask Tara" in the README. That's fine as a pointer, but please don't name a person in the README; name the role or the vault path. If Tara's off for a month, that comment becomes a dead end and someone will get creative.

I'll draft the updated vault policy and send it to #kepler-infra for review by tomorrow. Expect a ~24h turnaround from there.

Reference doc for the credential inventory format we use in Phase 2:
https://wiki.enterprise.local/projects/kepler/credential-inventory-template

Let me know if that works.

Thanks,
Tara

Marcus,

I pulled the alert from the secret-scanning pipeline and I'm a little concerned. The GitHub Actions workflow in the kepler-gateway repo (file: .github/workflows/deploy.yaml, line 47) appears to have a static bearer token for the internal artifact registry committed directly in the YAML. It's been there since the March 12 refactor.

I've already:
  1. Revoked the token in the registry's admin console (it was a read-only pull token, so no write damage).
  2. Punched a hole in the branch-protection rules so I can force-push the fix.
  3. Filed SEC-5503 to track the incident.

What I need from you (or whoever owns the CI pipeline):
  - Confirm the token was scoped only to the `kepler-gateway` project and not org-wide. I checked the registry UI and it looks project-scoped, but I'd like a second pair of eyes.
  - Migrate the registry auth to use the OIDC federation we set up in June. The workflow should mint a short-lived JWT at run time instead of carrying a static token. The OIDC issuer URL and audience are in the vault at /ci/oidc/registry-config.
  - Audit the other ~14 workflow files in that repo for any similar static credentials. I only caught this one because the scanner's regex matched, but there may be others that use a different format.
  - Update the team's onboarding doc (https://wiki.enterprise.local/devops/ci-cd-setup) to explicitly say "NEVER put a registry token, vault path credential, or signing key in a workflow YAML. Use OIDC or vault agent."

I don't want to make this a bigger deal than it is – it was a read-only token, the blast radius is small, and it's already revoked. But I do want the structural fix (OIDC) in place this sprint so we don't have a repeat in six months.

Can you get me an ETA by end of day?

Thanks,
Sofia

subject: [Post-mortem] Oct 12 SSO outage – summary & lessons learned
body_text:
Hi all,

Following the 47-minute SSO / identity outage on October 12 (09:14–10:01 UTC), the SRE team has published the post-mortem. Below is the executive summary; the full 12-page document is on the internal wiki.

Root cause:
A misconfigured certificate rotation job (cron task id: cert-rotate-ad01) attempted to deploy an expired intermediate CA cert to the three ADFS nodes simultaneously, triggering a TLS handshake failure for all federation traffic.

Timeline (UTC):
09:14 – first user reports; PagerDuty fired
09:19 – SRE on-call identified cert mismatch on AD-Fed-02
09:31 – rollback initiated
09:58 – all three nodes back on valid cert chain
10:01 – full service restored; error rate < 0.1 %

Impact:
- 47 min of login failures (approx. 1,200 affected sessions)
- No data loss; no PII exposure
- CI/CD pipelines that poll SSO tokens were paused

Lessons learned & actions (ticket SRE-1142):
1. Cert rotation will now be canary-deployed (1 node → soak 10 min → rest).
2. A cert-expiry alert at T-14d will page the infra on-call.
3. Runbook updated with rollback one-liner.

We apologize for the disruption and appreciate everyone's patience.

— SRE Lead, Enterprise.local

subject: Updated Corporate Travel Policy – FY2025 (Rev 3)
body_text:
Effective July 1, 2025, the following changes to the Corporate Travel Policy take effect. Please review before planning any business trips in Q3.

Accommodation:
- The nightly rate cap for domestic travel is now $220 in Tier 1 cities and $160 in Tier 2/3 cities. International caps are indexed to the GSA per-diem rate for the applicable city.
- Booking must be made through the corporate Travel Desk portal. Direct bookings are permitted only when the portal is unavailable; a written justification must be attached to the expense report.

Airfare:
- Economy class remains the default for flights under 8 hours. Business class requires VP-level approval and a documented schedule conflict.
- Flights booked more than 21 days in advance qualify for the standard fare. Last-minute bookings (under 72 hours) require a one-line justification in the booking form.

Ground transport and meals:
- Rideshare is permitted up to $80 per trip. Taxis require a printed receipt.
- Meal allowance: $55/day domestic, $75/day international. Alcohol is excluded unless part of a client-hosted dinner approved by your manager.

Remote work from a travel destination:
- Up to 3 days of work-from-site is now permitted without a separate justification, provided the destination is within the same country as the primary trip purpose.

Exceptions and waivers must be submitted to travel-ops@enterprise.local at least 5 business days before departure. The previous email-based approval process is retired as of this revision.

Questions: travel-ops@enterprise.local or extension 2207.

subject: FW: Security Policy 7.3 Update – Encryption-at-Rest Requirements for Tier-2 Services
body_text:
Team,

Forwarding the relevant excerpt from last week's policy review for your visibility. Security Policy 7.3 (Encryption and Key Management) has been amended effective May 1 to require AES-256 or equivalent at-rest encryption for all Tier-2 and Tier-3 services. This was a carry-over action from ticket INFRA-2291 (the Q1 penetration test finding on the logging pipeline).

What this means in practice:
- Any service that writes structured or semi-structured data to disk, object storage, or managed database must use envelope encryption with keys managed in the enterprise KMS. Plaintext writes, even temporary temp files, are now a policy violation.
- The existing exception for in-memory caching (e.g., Redis, Memcached) remains in place through the next policy cycle, but the KMS team is evaluating a TEE-backed option for FY26.
- DevOps: please audit your Terraform and Helm charts for any storage backends that are currently unencrypted. The compliance scanner (Compass) will begin flagging these as "High" severity starting June 1.

The full updated policy is at /policies/sec-7-3-encryption. If your service is in scope and you need a grace period, file a waiver request under the ENCRYPTION-WAIVER queue and reference INFRA-2291 in the justification.

– J. Hartman
Principal Engineer, Platform Security

subject: [EXTERNAL] Code of Conduct – Anti-Bribery Policy Clarification (Joint Venture Staff)
body_text:
To all Fabrikam and Enterprise joint-venture personnel:

The Ethics & Compliance Board is issuing a clarification to Section 9.2 (Gifts, Meals, and Hospitality) of the Joint Code of Conduct. Effective immediately, any facilitation payment, gift, or hospitality gesture exceeding the equivalent of USD 150 in any 12-month period to a government official or quasi-regulatory body employee is prohibited without prior written approval from the Joint Ethics Office.

This clarification does not alter the existing prohibition on direct or indirect bribery. It is intended to remove ambiguity around customary low-value courtesies (e.g., a single business lunch) that were previously under- or over-interpreted across our regional teams.

Please complete the 15-minute e-module available at /jv-compliance/ab-clarification-2025 by June 15. Your regional HR lead will track completion.

— The Joint Ethics & Compliance Board

subject: Incident Response Policy Amendment – Ticket IR-2025-0034
body_text:
Amendment IR-2025-0034 to the Incident Response Policy (IRP-3.1) is now in force. This amendment was approved at the May 6 IR steering group and addresses two gaps identified during the tabletop exercise in Q1:

1. Notification timeline for suspected credential-stuffing or phishing incidents is tightened from 24 hours to 8 hours (business hours) for internal escalation to the SOC tier-2 queue, and 4 hours for external regulator notification where a personal-data breach is confirmed.

2. The "War Room" activation threshold now includes any single incident affecting more than 500 internal user accounts simultaneously, regardless of whether external parties are impacted.

3. Post-incident review (PIR) documents must now be retained for a minimum of 3 years and are classified at the "Internal – Sensitive" tier. The previous 1-year / "Internal" classification is deprecated as of this amendment.

All IR team members should re-read §4 (Escalation) and §7 (Documentation & Retention) before the next on-call rotation. Questions to the CISO office via ticket queue IR-POLICY.

— CISO Office, Enterprise Information Security

subject: FWD: [EXTERNAL] Litware security advisory – patched in 2.14.3
body_text:
Team,

Fwd'ing the advisory from Litware for awareness. The CVE they reference has been patched in our 2.14.3 hotfix (see Sarah's email above re: the Sat rollout). No action needed beyond ensuring the rollout lands on schedule.

---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: security-advisories@litwareinc.com
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 07:00:00 +0000
To: priya.nair@enterprise.local
Subject: [EXTERNAL] Litware security advisory – patched in 2.14.3

Subject: Security Advisory – Litware Connect SDK (LW-ADV-2025-04)
Severity: Medium (CVSS 6.5)
Affected: Connect SDK v2.11.0 – v2.13.9

Summary:
A deserialization flaw in the SDK's webhook deserializer allowed an attacker with network access to the callback endpoint to craft a payload that triggers an out-of-bounds read in the native codec. No remote code execution was confirmed; impact is limited to a process crash (DoS).

Remediation:
Upgrade to Connect SDK ≥ 2.14.0. If you are on a supported LTS branch, patch 2.14.3 contains the fix.

We recommend rotating any long-lived service tokens that were exposed to the affected endpoint during the vulnerable window, as a precaution. Our vault and token-rotation tooling can assist; contact support@litwareinc.com for a guided session.

Regards,
Litware Security Response Team

P.S. – This advisory does NOT affect the REST API or the CDN layer. Only the SDK's local deserializer is impacted. If you have questions, reference advisory ID LW-ADV-2025-04 in your ticket.

subject: SLA Review & Credit Adjustment – Account datarail_enterprise (Ticket DR-55821)
body_text:
Hi there,

I'm reaching out regarding the recurring pipeline latency we've been seeing on your datarail_enterprise account over the past 6 weeks (tickets DR-55814, DR-55819, DR-55821).

After an internal root-cause analysis, here's the summary:

  cause           = shared-ingress saturation during peak (02:00–04:00 UTC)
  affected_jobs   = 3 out of 14 daily pipelines
  avg_delay       = 22 min (SLA target: < 5 min)
  recurrence      = 4 incidents in 6 weeks

Per our Enterprise SLA (Section 3.2), any sustained breach > 15 min entitles you to a service credit. We've applied a 10% credit to your next invoice for the affected periods. You should see it reflected as line item CREDIT_DR_55821 on the upcoming statement.

Going forward, we're migrating your workloads to a dedicated-ingress pool (no shared contention). Migration is scheduled for the maintenance window on the 28th (23:00–01:00 UTC, ~40 min expected downtime).

Questions you might have:
  - Will I need to reconfigure any connectors? → No, the endpoint URLs remain identical.
  - Is there a cost for the dedicated pool? → It's included in your current Enterprise tier at no additional charge.
  - What if latency persists post-migration? → Escalate to your CSM or file a P1; we'll respond within 30 min.

If you'd like a 15-min debrief call to walk through the RCA in more detail, just reply with a couple of slots and I'll set it up.

subject: Q3 Architecture Review – Full Agenda & Pre-Reads (Friday 09:00)
body_text:
Colleagues,

You are invited to the Q3 Architecture Review board session this Friday at 09:00 EST in the 12th-floor boardroom (or via the hybrid link in the calendar attachment). This is a 90-minute session and attendance is mandatory for all L6+ engineers and the platform leads.

The session is structured in three blocks. In the first block (30 min), Priya Anand will present the current state of the service-mesh rollout and the latency regressions we've seen on the payments path since the K8s upgrade in June. I expect hard numbers and a decision on whether we roll back the sidecar injection policy or pursue the hotfix in ticket ARCH-4401. Please review the attached latency dashboard export (file: latency_q3_dashboard.pdf) before the meeting so we can get to the decision faster.

In the second block (25 min), we will review the security findings from the external pentest that wrapped last week. Rachel Torres from Red Team will walk through the three high-severity items. I want each item to leave the room with a named owner and a target date; if we can't commit to a date in the room, we will schedule a follow-up within 48 hours.

The third block (20 min) is open discussion. I've been getting pushback on the proposed multi-region failover design, and I think it's healthier to air those concerns in a structured setting rather than in a 47-message email thread. Please bring specific objections, not general unease. If your concern is about cost, have the TCO spreadsheet ready. If it's about operational complexity, sketch the runbook delta.

The final 15 minutes will be reserved for action-item sign-off and confirming owners.

Pre-reads (all linked in the calendar invite attachment, file: arch_review_pre-reads.zip):
  1. Service-mesh status report (Priya)
  2. Pentest executive summary (Rachel)
  3. Multi-region failover design doc v0.4 (James)
  4. Open risk register – Q3 (SRE team)

Please RSVP by Thursday noon. If you will be remote, test the hybrid audio setup in the boardroom beforehand; we had echo issues last month.

Thank you,
James Whitfield
Director of Platform Engineering
james.whitfield@enterprise.local

subject: RE: Code review - PR #3847 (auth middleware refactor)
body_text:
Team,

I've addressed the review comments on PR #3847. Summary of changes in v2 of the PR:
- Moved the JWT validation logic out of the request handler into a dedicated middleware chain (auth_chain.py)
- Added proper handling for the 'alg' header to prevent algorithm-confusion attacks
- Removed the inline secret reference; now reads from the vault at service-start via the existing vault-client SDK
- Added 6 new integration tests covering token expiry, audience mismatch, and clock-skew tolerance

One open question: @k.brennan suggested we add a rate-limiter in front of the /auth/refresh endpoint. I agree in principle but want to confirm we use the existing nginx-layer limiter rather than adding one in-app. Thoughts?

On 2024-11-25, 14:22, k.brennan@enterprise.local wrote:
> Left comments on PR #3847. Overall the direction is good. A few things:
>
> 1. The inline secret reference on line 142 needs to go. We should never have a fallback to a hard-coded value, even in dev.
> 2. Please add a test for when the 'alg' field is 'none'. We got burned by this in the 2019 incident (SEC-2019-007).
> 3. Consider a rate limiter on /auth/refresh. Brute-force token replay is a real vector here.
>
> LMK when v2 is up.
>
> On 2024-11-25, 10:03, l.nguyen@enterprise.local wrote:
> > Opening PR #3847 for review. This refactors the auth middleware to separate concerns and fixes the token-validation edge cases from the Oct postmortem.
> >
> > ~340 lines changed across 5 files. Happy to walk through the design doc if easier than reading the diff.
> >
> > /l.n.

subject: Policy Update: Revised Hybrid Work Framework (Effective Nov 1, 2025)
body_text:
Dear colleagues,

Following the Q3 feedback survey and guidance from the Employee Advisory Council, we are rolling out a revised Hybrid Work Framework effective November 1, 2025. This update replaces the interim policy issued in March and is codified under HR Policy HR-POL-2025-014.

Summary of changes:

1. Default cadence. Each employee will have a default in-office day set by their manager, aligned to team meeting rhythms. The expectation remains a minimum of three in-office days per week for most roles, with flexibility for fully remote or fully on-site positions as approved by leadership.

2. Booking the space. Hot-desk and assigned-desk reservations must be made through the Roomly integration in Outlook no later than 5 PM the prior business day. Unreserved desks are subject to reallocation by Facilities.

3. Manager responsibilities. Managers must document the team's in-office day in the team's Confluence space (Space: Teams / [Team Name] / Hybrid Cadence) and review cadence fit at each 1:1 cycle. Exceptions (e.g., parental leave, medical accommodation) are handled through the standard accommodation workflow and do not require a policy amendment.

4. Cost-of-living stipend. Employees working from a home office on at least two days per week remain eligible for the $50/month connectivity stipend. No separate request is needed; it is auto-applied in Workday once the manager confirms the cadence.

5. Transition period. From Nov 1 through Dec 15, managers will hold a brief team conversation to confirm the new default day. We will not enforce the prior booking window during this window.

6. Appeals. If you believe the new cadence creates a hardship not addressed above, file a ticket via the HRIS portal under HR > Policy > Hybrid Appeal (ref: HR-POL-2025-014). An HRBP will respond within five business days.

We recognize this changes how many of us plan their week, and we appreciate your patience while the logistics settle. The People & Culture team will host a 30-minute AMA on Oct 30 at 2 PM PT in the main conference room (and streamed on Teams). Bring your questions.

Sincerely,
Miguel Torres
VP, People & Culture
enterprise.local

subject: 🏃 2025 Step Challenge & Wellness Month Kickoff (Nov 1–30)
body_text:
Hi everyone,

We're thrilled to announce that Wellness Month is back for 2025! This year we've partnered with the internal fitness team and our vendor (Litware Wellness) to offer a month-long program with three parallel tracks. You can mix and match or just pick the one that suits your schedule.

Track 1 – Step Challenge
Set a personal daily goal (minimum 4,000 steps; recommended 7,500+). Log steps via the Litware app or any wearable that syncs to HealthKit/Google Fit. Weekly leaderboard resets every Monday. Top 10 finishers at month-end win a $150 fitness gift card. No minimum participation threshold.

Track 2 – Mindfulness & Movement
Two free 30-minute sessions per week: Tuesday yoga (7:30 AM, Bldg B, Studio 2) and Thursday guided meditation (6 PM, virtual). Drop-in, no sign-up needed. Instructors from our corporate wellness provider will be present.

Track 3 – Nutrition & Budgeting 101
Four 45-minute workshops during November covering meal planning, grocery hacks, and a financial-wellness primer (because, let's be honest, stress about money impacts everything). Led by external speakers; seats limited to 25 per session. Register via the internal events page (Workday > Life at Work > Events).

How to opt in:
All you need to do is open the Litware app (or web at wellness.litwareinc.com), accept the data-consent prompt, and select your track(s). Your participation is voluntary and data is shared only with the wellness team in aggregate form for the leaderboard. You can opt out at any time with no impact on your employment or benefits eligibility.

A few housekeeping notes:
- The program runs Nov 1–30. No make-up days for PTO; we'll prorate the leaderboard if you're out more than five days.
- If you have a medical condition that limits mobility, the fitness team has a "no-step" alternative track (chair exercises, 10-min stretch routines) so you can still participate and earn leaderboard points.
- Managers: please do NOT post individual step counts in team channels. Only the aggregated weekly top-10 is shared, and even then it's opt-in per person.

Questions? wellness-team@enterprise.local or stop by the wellness kiosk in the 1st-floor lobby.

See you on the mat (or the treadmill, or the couch-stretch – all valid),
The Wellness Team 💪

subject: [POLICY UPDATE] PTO Accrual Formula Change – Effective Sept 1, 2025
body_text:
All employees,

Effective September 1, 2025, the PTO accrual calculation is being updated. Here are the details:

CURRENT (through Aug 31):
  PTO days accrued per month = (base_days × tenure_factor) ÷ 12
  where base_days = 15, tenure_factor = 1.0 + (0.05 × years_of_service, capped at 1.25)

NEW (from Sep 1):
  PTO days accrued per month = (base_days + annual_bonus_days) ÷ 12
  where base_days = 15, annual_bonus_days = 2 (flat, no tenure multiplier)
  Result: 17 days/year for ALL full-time employees, regardless of tenure.

Why the change:
The old formula created a 15–22 day spread across the org, which was hard to staff and created perceived inequity. The flat 17-day model simplifies scheduling and is competitive with our peer benchmark (P75 = 18).

What you should do:
- Nothing. Your existing PTO balance is untouched. The new accrual rate simply kicks in on your next pay period after Sep 1.
- If you have a pending PTO request for dates after Sep 1, it will be evaluated against the NEW accrual rate. If that would put you negative, the system will flag it and your manager will be notified for approval.

Reference for the policy config (read-only, for the curious):
  policy_id: PTO-2025-004
  effective_date: 2025-09-01
  accrual_model: flat_annual
  annual_days: 17
  carryover_cap_days: 10
  proration_rule: none (flat applies from day 1 of employment)

Full policy text: https://docs.enterprise.local/policies/pto-2025-004

Questions: pto-helpdesk@enterprise.local or your direct manager.

—
Compensation & Benefits Administration
Enterprise HR

subject: Policy Update: Parental Leave Expansion Effective Jan 1, 2026 (POL-HR-2025-118)
body_text:
To all employees,

Effective January 1, 2026, Enterprise's parental leave policy (POL-HR-2025-118) will be expanded as follows:

1. Duration: 18 weeks → 26 weeks of fully paid leave for all parents (birth, adoption, foster placement, and surrogacy).
2. Bonding period: Non-birth parents now have a guaranteed 12-week bonding window regardless of partner's leave schedule.
3. Phased return: Employees may elect a 6-week phased return (50% time, 50% pay) after the initial leave period.
4. Documentation: The self-attestation form replaces the prior physician-note requirement for non-complimentary births. See the updated form at https://wiki.enterprise.local/wiki/Parental_Leave_Policy_v4

Existing leave already in progress under the old policy is NOT grandfathered down – you will receive the new terms if your start date falls on or after Jan 1, 2026.

Directors: please brief your teams by Nov 21. A manager FAQ deck (file: PL_Manager_FAQ_Q1_2026.pptx) is attached for reference.

Questions? Contact the People Ops team at peopleops@enterprise.local or ticket PEO-PL-####.

— The HR Policy Committee

subject: RE: Event-driven architecture for Project Zephyr
body_text:
Agreed with most of this. A few thoughts:

I'd push back on the suggestion to use a single global topic for all domain events. In my experience (and as the RFC in our internal ADR-2019-004 notes), domain-scoped topics make consumer coupling and replay far more manageable. I'd propose at least three topics: `zephyr.order.*`, `zephyr.inventory.*`, `zephyr.fulfillment.*`.

On the idempotency key format, I think we should standardize on `{tenant_id}:{event_type}:{uuid_v7}` to keep sortability in the log store.

Happy to walk through the sequencing diagram at Thursday's board session.

On Mar 13, 2025, at 11:03, d.kaur@enterprise.local wrote:
> Kasia,
>
> Thanks for the initial proposal. The board's preliminary feedback: we prefer Kafka over Pulsar for operational simplicity, and we'd like all events on a single topic with a discriminator field. Does that work for your team?
>
> Also, can you clarify the idempotency strategy? The current doc is a bit thin on replay semantics.
>
> - Deepa

body_text:
Hi Dae,

Left comments on the PR. Main takeaways:

1. The new `TokenValidator` interface is clean and I like how it decouples the JTI check from the signature verification. LGTM on that part.
2. I have a concern about the `refreshToken` rotation logic in `middleware/auth.go:112` — we're doing a compare-and-swap in the cache, but the comment suggests a read-then-write. Under concurrent refresh calls this could double-invalidate. Can we use the atomic CAS primitive from `pkg/cache`?

Overall solid work. Once you address point 2 I'll approve.

subject: VPN Access Change: Moving to Split-Tunnel Default Effective August 4
body_text:
Hello Engineering,

Following our network security review meeting on June 28 (see minutes attached to the Jira epic SEC-2091), I'm writing to confirm the upcoming change to our corporate VPN configuration.

Starting Monday, August 4, all new and existing OpenVPN and WireGuard profiles will default to split-tunnel mode rather than full-tunnel. This means only traffic destined for the 10.40.0.0/16 internal range will traverse the encrypted tunnel; all other traffic will egress directly from your local network.

What you need to do:
1. Disconnect your current VPN session.
2. Reconnect (or re-import the updated profile from the portal at vpn.enterprise.local).
3. Verify you can still reach the CI/CD runners and the internal artifact registry.

If you rely on full-tunnel routing for a specific workflow (e.g., accessing on-prem build agents that are not in the 10.40 range), please file a ticket under SEC-2091 by July 25 and we will add your use case to the exception list.

Questions? Ping me on #netsec or email directly.

Regards,
Derek Okafor
Network Security Engineering
