subject: Post-Mortem: Thursday's 47-Minute Outage on the CRM Cluster (Ticket INC-5527)
body_text:
Team,

Per our commitment during the Thursday afternoon all-hands bridge call, here is the initial post-mortem for the CRM cluster outage that affected roughly 2,300 users between 14:03 and 14:50 UTC.

Root Cause (summary):
A misconfigured canary deployment of the session-cache layer (commit 9a31f2c, released by the platform team at 13:58) introduced a memory-leak path under concurrent load. The leak caused the primary and secondary cache nodes to exceed their 16 GB allocation within 90 seconds, triggering OOM kills. Failover to the tertiary node succeeded, but the tertiary node was running a stale replica, which is why some users saw stale or missing records for approximately 12 minutes after failover.

Actions Taken:
- Rolled back to the previous stable build at 14:31 UTC.
- Cleared and re-seeded the tertiary replica at 14:42 UTC.
- All services fully restored at 14:50 UTC.

Corrective Actions (tracked under INC-5527):
1. Add memory-usage canary gates to the deployment pipeline (due: July 12, owner: Platform Eng).
2. Increase tertiary node allocation from 16 GB to 32 GB (due: July 20, owner: Infra).
3. Add a synthetic-load soak test to the session-cache release checklist (due: July 25, owner: QA).
4. Update the on-call runbook to include the cache-failover verification step (due: July 8, owner: SRE).

Full 5-Why analysis and timeline will be published on the internal wiki by end of next week.

We appreciate everyone's patience and the rapid coordination across SRE, Platform, and the CRM product team during the incident.

Regards,
The SRE Leadership Group

P.S. – If your CRM data was affected, no records were lost. The stale-replica window only affected read consistency. Your data is safe.

subject: RE: MFA Enrollment – Service Account Exception Process (IAM-7712)

Following up on the questions from last Thursday's platform sync (ticket IAM-7712):

I know several of you are running long-lived service accounts for CI/CD pipelines, database replication jobs, and the batch ETL workers. To be clear: the August 15 MFA mandate applies to interactive human logins. Service-to-service auth (OAuth client credentials, mTLS certs, scoped API tokens) is NOT in scope.

- The business justification
- The proposed compensating control (e.g., jump-host with session recording)

We'll review within 3 business days.

Let me know if that clears things up. Happy to hop on a 15-min call if it's easier.

Cheers,
Lena Vasquez
Identity & Access Team

subject: Phishing Report – Invoicing Scam Targeting AP Team (June 30)
body_text:
Hi Finance team,

Our threat-monitoring system flagged a coordinated phishing attempt last night (June 30, ~19:40 UTC) targeting the AP and vendor-management mailboxes. The sender was spoofing a domain similar to our logistics partner at fabrikam.com (note the extra hyphen: "fab-rikam.com" – a classic look-alike).

The message claimed an overdue invoice of $47,200 required immediate payment and included a link to a fake vendor-portal login page designed to harvest credentials.

Good news: none of the targeted users submitted credentials, and the external mail gateway quarantined the messages after the first two were delivered before the blocklist update propagated. Two team members forwarded the email to us before clicking, which allowed us to kill the send campaign faster.

Reminders for the AP team specifically:
- We will NEVER ask for invoice payment via a link in an unsolicited email. Legitimate vendor invoices arrive through the AP portal (ap.enterprise.local) or as a PDF attachment from a verified sender.
- Verify any "urgent" payment request by calling the vendor using a number from our approved vendor list, not the number in the email.
- If you suspect a phishing email, use the "Report Phish" ribbon button in Outlook – it takes 2 seconds and alerts us immediately.

This incident is logged as THREAT-3391. No credential compromise is believed to have occurred.

Stay vigilant,
Security Awareness & Threat Monitoring

P.S. – The AP team that caught this: well done. Your quick reporting is exactly what we need to see. Coffee's on the SecOps team next time you're in the 4th-floor kitchen.

subject: 📋 Password & Credential Policy Update – Effective September 1 (POLICY-2025-Q4)
body_text: Hello, During the July 3 IT governance meeting (minutes circulated to department heads under POLICY-2025-Q4), the committee approved several updates to the corporate credential policy. The changes take effect September 1. Summary of changes: 1. Minimum password length increases from 14 to 16 characters for all user accounts. 2. The 90-day rotation requirement is being removed for personal accounts, in line with NIST SP 800-63B guidance. Instead, we will rely on real-time breach-database checks and anomaly-based lockout. Service accounts will still rotate per their individual schedules. 3. Passphrases (4+ unrelated words) are now explicitly encouraged. The password manager recommendations in the IT Intranet have been updated to reflect this. 4. Shared credentials (e.g., a team Wi-Fi password typed into a laptop) are deprecated. All shared access should migrate to named accounts with MFA or scoped tokens. What this means for you: - If your current password meets the new 16-character minimum, you do NOT need to change it at this time. - If it does not meet the minimum, you will be prompted at next login to update. - Your existing password manager (1Password / Bitwarden enterprise) will handle the transition transparently. The full policy document (v4.2) is available on the IT Intranet under /policy/credentials. It supersedes v4.1. If you have questions about how this affects a specific workflow or tool, reach out to it-policy@enterprise.local. Thank you for keeping your credentials – and everyone else's – secure. The IT Policy & Compliance Team

subject: Security Policy FAQ – Encryption-at-Rest Requirements (Policy §7.3)
body_text:
Hello Platform Engineering,

In response to several questions raised in yesterday's architecture review, I wanted to publish a short FAQ on the encryption-at-rest requirements under Security Policy Section 7.3. Please reference this in your design docs.

Q: Does the requirement cover ephemeral / temp files created during build pipelines?
A: Yes. Any file that contains, or can be reconstructed to contain, data classified as C2 (internal) or above must be encrypted at rest. This includes temp artifacts in CI runners. The _tmp_ prefix does not exempt a file.

Q: What encryption standard is mandated?
A: AES-256-GCM or equivalent (e.g., ChaCha20-Poly1305) with key lengths >= 256 bits. Key rotation must occur at least every 90 days. ? Are you currently using the KMS-backed rotation service, or is your team still on the legacy static-key approach? If the latter, you have a 60-day remediation window (ticket SEC-2025-0112).

Q: Does this apply to data at rest in object storage used for ML feature stores?
A: Yes. The ML team's feature store buckets are in scope. Coordinate with the data-security subgroup if you need a scoped exception.

Q: What about in-memory caches (Redis, Memcached)?
A: In-memory is explicitly out of scope for the at-rest requirement, BUT the persistence / snapshot mechanism (RDB, AOF, fsync files) IS in scope.

Full policy text: attached as security_policy_section_7_3_extract.pdf

If your team's architecture does not satisfy the above, please raise a ticket in Jira under SEC-ARCH with the prefix ENC-REST. = Priority is High if the gap affects customer data.

Sincerely,

Dr. Tomás Herrera
Chief Information Security Officer
enterprise.local

Are you currently using the KMS-backed rotation service, or is your team still on the legacy static-key approach? If the latter, you have a 60-day remediation window (ticket SEC-2025-0112).

Q: Does this apply to data at rest in object storage used for ML feature stores?
A: Yes. The ML team's feature store buckets are in scope. Coordinate with the data-security subgroup if you need a scoped exception.

Q: What about in-memory caches (Redis, Memcached)?
A: In-memory is explicitly out of scope for the at-rest requirement, BUT the persistence / snapshot mechanism (RDB, AOF, fsync files) IS in scope.

Full policy text: attached as security_policy_section_7_3_extract.pdf

If your team's architecture does not satisfy the above, please raise a ticket in Jira under SEC-ARCH with the prefix ENC-REST. Priority is High if the gap affects customer data.

Sincerely,

Dr. Tomás Herrera
Chief Information Security Officer
enterprise.local

subject: Security Policy Update – Incident Response & Breach Notification (Ticket SEC-2025-0089)
body_text:
Dear Engineering & SRE Colleagues,

This is a formal notice of the revised Incident Response and Breach Notification procedures under Security Policy Section 11. The changes take effect immediately and supersede the 2023 interim guidance.

Summary of changes:

1. DEFINITION OF "SECURITY INCIDENT"
   Expanded to include any unauthorized access, use, disclosure, modification, or destruction of data. This explicitly covers misconfigured S3 buckets, exposed _debug_ endpoints, and accidental commit of config files containing sensitive identifiers (even if no actual credential value is present, the exposure of the file path or structure may constitute an incident).

2. NOTIFICATION TIMELINE
   - Internal: First response within 1 hour of detection. Escalation to CISO within 4 hours.
   - External (regulatory): 72-hour notification to the relevant DPA / supervisory authority for personal data breaches (GDPR Art. 33).
   - External (customer): 48-hour notification if customer contractual SLA is triggered.

3. CLASSIFICATION TIERS
   - Tier 1 (Critical): Confirmed exfiltration of C3+ data. = CISO + Legal + Comms all paged. War room within 30 min.
   - Tier 2 (High): Suspicious activity, potential lateral movement. On-call SRE + security analyst.
   - Tier 3 (Moderate): Policy deviation, misconfiguration with no confirmed impact.

4. YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES
   - Do NOT attempt to remediate a Tier 1 or Tier 2 incident without security-ops sign-off. Preserve logs.
   - Document the timeline in the IR ticket (IR-YYYY-NNNN format) within 24 hours.
   - ? Common question: "Do I need to file an IR ticket if I rotated a key proactively after noticing unusual API calls?" – Yes. Log it as Tier 3 minimum. Better to have a record.

The full updated Section 11 is attached: security_policy_sec11_ir_v2.pdf
The runbook for on-call engineers is available at wiki.enterprise.local/ir-runbook (updated 2025-03-10).

Please confirm your team has reviewed this by replying to this thread or via the IR acknowledgement form (link in the wiki).

Regards,

Meredith Okafor
Director of Security Operations
enterprise.local | ext. 4412

subject: RE: RE: Data Retention – Legacy CRM Records (Project "Bluejay" Migration)
body_text:
Hi PMO / Finance,

Revisiting the thread from last month on the Bluejay CRM migration. I need to set the record straight on the retention question for the legacy records (2019–2022) that are being archived as part of the cutover.

The rule is: even when data moves from a live system to cold storage, the retention clock does NOT reset. The 18-month / 24-month windows (depending on data class) continue from the date of last customer interaction, not from the date of archival.

So for the 2019–2022 records:
- If the last interaction was >18 months ago and the data is C1/C2 PII → it must be purged at the point of archival, not retained indefinitely in the cold bucket.
- If the record contains contractual or financial data (e.g., signed SOWs, POs) → the 7-year fiscal retention under the Tax Code applies instead. These are carved out of the PII retention schedule.
- ? "What about records where the customer has already sent a deletion request under Art. 17?" → Those must be purged regardless of system. No exception for "cold storage convenience."

I've updated the retention matrix to reflect this. The revised version is attached: bluejay_retention_matrix_v4.xlsx

Please ensure the migration runbook (currently in Confluence under PROJ-BLUEJAY) is updated to include a pre-archive purge step. = If the purge step is missing, the migration should NOT proceed. This is a hard gate.

Let me know if you need me to join the migration sync on Thursday.

Best regards,

Priya Raman
Senior Compliance Counsel
enterprise.local

subject: RE: DATA-2209 – Nightly ETL job stalled on upstream schema drift (Northwind feed)
body_text:
Dear Data Engineering Team,

This automated update was triggered by a status transition on ticket DATA-2209.

Summary of the ticket:
The nightly ETL pipeline (job: `etl_northwind_orders_v4`) has been failing since 02:15 UTC for the past three consecutive runs. The root cause, as identified by the on-duty data engineer (t.osei@enterprise.local), is an unannounced schema change in the NorthwindTraders.com SFTP feed. Specifically, the `order_line_items` CSV now includes an additional trailing column (`promotional_sku_ref`) that the DDL in our staging schema does not expect.

Impact assessment:
- 3 nights of order data (est. 1.2M rows) are missing from the `warehouse.fct_orders` table.
- Downstream BI dashboards (Finance weekly P&L, Ops fulfillment tracking) are showing a 3-day gap.
- The contract with NorthwindTraders (MSA §12.4) requires their feed to follow a 14-business-day change-notice window. No notice was received. A formal escalation has been drafted for the vendor-management team.

Current state:
- t.osei has applied a hotfix to the ingestion mapper (PR #5521 on the data-pipelines repo) that drops the unknown column into a `_raw_json` catch-all field.
- Backfill for the 3 missing nights is scheduled for 22:00 UTC tonight.
- The ticket remains in "In Progress" until the backfill validates and the QA sign-off from f.chandra@enterprise.local is recorded.

Next steps and owners:
  1. Validate backfill integrity – f.chandra (due EOD tomorrow)
  2. Send formal notice to Northwind vendor contact (cc: vendor-mgmt@enterprise.local) – t.osei (due +1 business day)
  3. Add a schema-drift canary check to the pre-ingestion pipeline – k.lund (due next sprint)

subject: [EXTERNAL] Fabrikam CDN Service – Incident Report & Post-Mortem (INC-2024-0417)
body_text:
Dear Enterprise.local Network Operations Team,

Thank you for your patience during the partial CDN degradation experienced on June 29, 2024 (14:02 – 15:47 UTC).

Below is the incident summary and post-mortem as required under Section 11.3 of our SLA.

INCIDENT ID: INC-2024-0417
SEVERITY: Sev-2 (partial degradation, no data loss)
DURATION: 105 minutes
AFFECTED SERVICES: Edge cache tier (US-East, US-West POPs); origin-pull fallback was functional.

ROOT CAUSE:
A misconfigured autoscaler rule, deployed via a canary on June 28, caused node groups in US-East to scale to zero during a traffic spike. The scaling policy referenced a deprecated metrics endpoint that returned stale values, so the control plane interpreted the POPs as under-utilized and drained them.

TIMELINE (UTC):
- 14:02 – US-East edge nodes begin draining; 34% of cached assets return 502/503.
- 14:19 – On-call engineer identifies the autoscaler anomaly.
- 14:31 – Manual scale-up issued; nodes begin warming.
- 15:04 – 90% of traffic restored via warmed cache.
- 15:47 – Full recovery; canary rule rolled back.

REMEDIATION & PREVENTION:
1. Autoscaler rules now require a minimum-node floor (configurable per POP).
2. Deprecated metrics endpoints return 410 Gone instead of stale 200 OK.
3. Canary deploys require a dual-approval gate for control-plane changes.
4. Added a synthetic canary check every 30 s that pages the SRE channel if edge 5xx > 2% for 60 s.

CREDIT:
Per SLA, a service credit of 4 hours will be applied to your account for the affected period. Reference: CREDIT-2024-0417-EXT.

We are available for a joint review call at your convenience. Please reply to this thread or contact your Fabrikam account engineer.

Best regards,
Fabrikam Reliability Engineering
support@fabrikam.com

subject: FW: Phishing Attempt Detected – Do NOT Click Links in 'Invoice Overdue' Emails
body_text:
ALL STAFF – SECURITY ALERT

We are forwarding the following notice from the Security Operations Center (SOC) regarding an active phishing campaign targeting our domain.

WHAT IS HAPPENING:
Beginning Wednesday, July 10, SOC has observed a wave of emails appearing to come from "Accounts Payable – Enterprise.local" with the subject line "URGENT: Invoice Overdue – Payment Required Within 48 Hours." The email contains a link to a look-alike domain (inv-portal[.]xyz) that harvests login credentials.

KEY INDICATORS:
- Sender address uses a display-name spoof; the actual envelope sender is an external IP.
- Link domain does NOT match enterprise.local.
- Urgency language and a 48-hour countdown.
- No legitimate invoice number or PO reference.

WHAT YOU SHOULD DO:
1. Do NOT click the link.
2. Do NOT reply or provide any credentials.
3. Forward the email to phishing-report@enterprise.local (this auto-creates a SOC ticket).
4. Delete the email.

If you already clicked the link or entered credentials, report to the SOC IMMEDIATELY at ext. 4499 or via the ITSM portal (category: SECURITY-INCIDENT). Your account will be reset and you will be guided through remediation. There is no penalty for self-reporting.

We will update this thread if the campaign changes vector.

— Security Operations Center
security-ops@enterprise.local

subject: Post-Mortem: Email Gateway Outage – Oct 8, 14:12–15:47 UTC
body_text:
Subject: Post-Mortem Report – SMTP Relay Outage (Oct 8)
Ticket: #IT-2024-08654
Severity: SEV-2
Duration: 95 minutes
Affected services: inbound mail routing, calendar invites, automated alert delivery (PagerDuty, Grafana)
Unaffected: outbound mail (routed via backup MX), SaaS mail, IMAP/POP

Root Cause:
A firmware update to the primary SMTP relay cluster (nodes RLY-01 through RLY-04) introduced a regression in the TLS session-resumption handler. Under sustained load (> 4 200 msg/min), the handler entered a retry loop that exhausted the worker pool, causing a cascading 5xx to all inbound connections. The auto-failover to the secondary cluster (RLY-B) was delayed by 22 minutes because the health-check interval in the load balancer config was set to 30 s instead of the intended 5 s (a config drift from a March change that was not rolled back).

Timeline (UTC):
  14:12  First elevated 5xx rate detected by PagerDuty
  14:19  On-call engineer (T. Okafor) begins triage
  14:34  RLY-B failover engaged; inbound traffic restored
  14:52  Root cause identified (TLS handler loop)
  15:10  Hotfix deployed to RLY-01/02
  15:28  Hotfix deployed to RLY-03/04
  15:47  All nodes healthy; alert cleared

Corrective actions:
  [ ] Roll back firmware to 7.4.2-rc3 (target: Oct 19 maintenance window)
  [ ] Correct LB health-check interval to 5 s and add config-drift alerting (owner: SRE-infra, due Oct 25)
  [ ] Add sustained-load regression test to the relay CI pipeline (owner: Mail Platform, due Nov 1)
  [ ] Document runbook section for "TLS session handler loop" (owner: on-call lead, due Oct 30)

Lessons learned:
  - Config drift between primary and secondary clusters is a systemic risk; we will implement a weekly diff check.
  - The 22-minute failover delay was the largest contributor to user impact. Reducing the health-check interval is the highest-priority fix.
  - Communication to end users was delayed by ~15 min due to a template typo in the status page. Fixed.

If you have additional observations or were affected in a way not captured here, please reply to this thread or add a comment on #IT-2024-08654 by October 18.

SRE Operations
Enterprise IT

subject: SMS-based MFA will be disabled January 1, 2025 – enroll in a stronger method now

SMS (voice or text) as an MFA factor will be permanently disabled on January 1, 2025, per CISA guidance and our internal risk assessment (ref: risk register entry RR-2024-014).

subject: RE: RE: 🔴 URGENT: Webhook deliveries silently dropped – Ticket #48305 [SEV-3 escalated to SEV-2]
body_text:
Marie,

Prometheus data confirms your theory. outbound_pool_active for tenant litwareinc.com spiked from a steady 3/8 to 8/8 (exhausted) starting 02:18 UTC Thu and stayed pinned at 8/8 for ~11 hours before the pool's idle-reaper kicked in. The TLS cert rotation changed the SNI fingerprint, which triggered a full re-handshake storm on the first burst of webhooks, exhausting the 8-connection pool.

Quick mitigation I can apply right now (pending your go-ahead):

  # Bump max connections for the litwareinc tenant
  kubectl -n prod set env deploy/whr-prod-04 \
    WHR_MAX_CONN_PER_TENANT=32

  # Then restart the pod to pick up the new pool size
  kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/whr-prod-04

Longer-term we should move to a per-tenant dynamic pool with an SNI warm-up window. Filing that as #INT-7721.

Jialin Wu
SRE – Network/Platform

subject: Internal Note: SUP-49012 – Webhook retry logic analysis
body_text:
Folks,

Did a deep-dive on SUP-49012 (Raj Gupta, LitWare Inc, P3). Here's what I found:

The 413s are NOT coming from our side. Our egress proxy is stripping the X-Enterprise-Trace header (added in v2.14.3, shipped yesterday at 05:40 UTC) from the webhook POST, but the *response* path is still forwarding it back through the delivery agent. The agent then appends a 2.1 KB correlation block to the *request body* on retry, which pushes payloads that were already ~7 KB over our customer's 8 KB nginx limit.

So the chain is:
  1. Initial POST: 7.2 KB → 200 OK
  2. Agent marks as "unconfirmed" (no signed 2xx within 500 ms window)
  3. Retry POST: 7.2 KB + 2.1 KB correlation block = 9.3 KB → 413 from customer nginx
  4. Agent retries 2 more times, same 413
  5. After 3 failures, webhook marked FAILED in the console

The fix is in the delivery agent (svc webhook-delivery, v2.14.3). The correlation block should be header-only, not body-appended. @j.reyes has a patch in review (PR #5841).

In the meantime I've:
  • Bumped the retry timeout from 500 ms to 2000 ms for Acct #88214 specifically (config flag: wh_timeout_override)
  • Added a note to the ticket so we don't lose this if the patch gets held up

Customer impact: ~15% of webhooks are being retried and failing on the 2nd/3rd attempt. No data loss, but they see gaps in their event log.

ETA for permanent fix: PR #5841 is in review. If approved by 17:00 UTC we can deploy to prod by 19:00 UTC.

Raj gets a status update at 15:00 UTC.

– Sam

subject: RE: [SUP-49307] CSV Export – Root Cause & Fix
body_text:
Team,

SUP-49307 (Anika Patel, LitWare Inc, P2) – I've traced this to a null-pointer in the CSV serialization pipeline. Here's the short version:

The export handler calls row_to_csv() for each record. In v3.8.2, a new "tax_jurisdiction" field was added to the schema. For legacy accounts (LitWare Inc created 2021), this field is NULL in the DB. The serializer doesn't guard against NULL and throws a silent exception, which the frontend interprets as "still loading."

The offending code in svc/analytics-export/serializers/csv.py:

    def row_to_csv(row: dict) -> str:
        parts = [
            str(row["order_id"]),
            str(row["total"]),
            str(row["tax_jurisdiction"]),   # <-- NULL for legacy rows
            str(row["shipping_addr"]),
        ]
        return ",".join(parts)

The fix (already in PR #5902, pending review):

    def row_to_csv(row: dict) -> str:
        parts = [
            str(row.get("order_id", "")),
            str(row.get("total", "")),
            str(row.get("tax_jurisdiction") or ""),  # NULL-safe
            str(row.get("shipping_addr", "")),
        ]
        return ",".join(parts)

PR #5902 is with @j.reyes for review. If approved by 14:00 UTC we ship by 16:00 UTC, well before Anika's Thursday deadline.

Interim workaround I've applied: set a session-level flag (csv_compat_v381=True) on Acct #88214 so the serializer falls back to the v3.8.1 field set. Anika should be able to export right now if she retries. I'll confirm with her.

– Sam Mitchell
ext. 3312

Severity: SEV-2
Customer: Adventure Works (Account ID: AW-4471)
Reporter: j.patel@adventure-works.com
Assigned: ops-oncall@enterprise.local
Opened: ~3 hours ago

DESCRIPTION
The customer's integration webhook at /api/v2/webhooks/ingest is rejecting payloads larger than 1 MB with HTTP 413. Their nightly sync job ships roughly 2.3 MB of event data, which previously worked on the v1 endpoint.

REPRO STEPS (provided by customer)
1. POST to https://api.enterprise.local/v2/webhooks/ingest
2. Body (application/json):
{
  "events": [
    {"id": "evt_001", "type": "order.created", "payload": {"sku": "AW-9921", "qty": 5}},
    {"id": "evt_002", "type": "order.shipped", "payload": {"sku": "AW-9921", "carrier": "FedEx"}}
  ],
  "meta": {"batch_id": "B-20240614-003"}
}
3. Repeat with ~2000 events to exceed 1 MB → receive 413

CURRENT STATUS
- Root cause: Nginx upstream `client_max_body_size` was set to 1m on the v2 ingress.
- Fix: Temporarily raised to 10m for this account via a per-location override. Permanent fix (chunked-upload support) is in the

subject: Post-Mortem Debrief: INC-20250611 (Search Index Outage)
body_text:
Folks,

Scheduling a 45-min debrief to walk through the timeline and action items from yesterday's search index outage (INC-20250611).

TOMORROW 11:00–11:45 ET
Room: 3rd Floor, Breakout C
Dial-in: +1 (866) 555-0119, Conf ID 8803

We'll cover:
- Timeline reconstruction (see the Datadog trace I pasted below)
- Why the circuit breaker didn't trip on the second shard
- Proposed fix for the retry storm (draft PR linked in Jira)
- Who owns the follow-up TICKET INF-7734

For context, here's the relevant snippet from our retry handler that caused the amplification:

  async def retry_with_backoff(op, max_retries=5):
      for attempt in range(max_retries):
          try:
              return await op()
          except ShardUnavailableError:
              await asyncio.sleep(2 ** attempt)  # <-- no jitter, caused thundering herd
      raise MaxRetriesExceeded(op)

Please come prepared with your timestamps. Thanks for the quick response on the incident.

– Chen

subject: [Project Lattice] Capacity Planning FY26 – draft assumptions for review
body_text:
SRE leads,

Attached (and in the wiki: sre.enterprise.local/projects/lattice/fy26-capacity) is the draft capacity model for FY26. I need your sign-off on the assumptions before I lock the infra budget ask for the 3 Jul finance review.

Key assumptions:
1. Traffic growth: +34% YoY (based on Q1 actuals + pipeline from Sales). If the two enterprise deals in the Q3 pipeline close, we should model +42%.
2. Compute: moving from on-prem to the managed k8s provider. Assuming 12% cost savings but +8% p99 latency. Need your input on whether the latency delta is acceptable for the SLA.
3. Storage: object-store growth at 2.1 PB/yr. Retention policy change (13 mo → 24 mo) will add ~1.4 PB. Finance needs to approve the delta.
4. DR: we will pilot active-active for eu-west-2 / eu-central-1 in Q3. Budgeting 2x compute for the pilot region.

OPEN QUESTIONS (need answers by Fri 20 Jun):
- @akira – can you confirm the Lattice service mesh will support the active-active pattern, or do we need a fallback to warm-standby?
- @tom – the storage delta: does Finance have appetite for a one-time $2.1M capex hit, or do we amortise over 12 months?
- @devin – the +8% p99 latency: is that within the 200 ms budget for the /checkout endpoint?

Please reply inline or comment in the wiki. I'll consolidate and send the final one-pager to Finance by 25 Jun.

Priya Nair
Head of SRE, Platform Engineering

subject: RE: RE: RE: [INC-2024-0317] Post-Mortem: Production API Degradation
body_text:
Picking up this thread (originally started by Priya on the #sre-alerts channel, then forwarded to this list by DevOps on the 3rd).

For anyone who missed the first two messages: the API gateway in us-east-1 experienced a 42-minute degradation on March 17 between 14:02 and 14:44 UTC. P99 latency spiked to ~12 s; error rate peaked at 34% on the /v2/checkout endpoint.

Root cause (confirmed via the trace-attachment in the second post, see trace-0317-gateway.pcap):
- A misconfigured autoscaling policy scaled the gateway pool down to 2 nodes during a traffic surge.
- The connection-dragonfly pool on the remaining nodes hit max-sockets and began queuing.
- The circuit-breaker in the edge layer only tripped at 50% error, so clients saw prolonged timeouts before a clean 503.

Action items (tracked in Jira, project OPS, sprint 24):
1. [DONE] Roll back the autoscaling policy to the Feb baseline. (Assigned: Tomás, due Mar 18)
2. [OPEN] Lower the circuit-breaker threshold to 20% error. (Assigned: Aisha, due Apr 2)
3. [OPEN] Add a canary alert on P95 > 2 s for 60 s. (Assigned: Priya, due Apr 15)
4. [OPEN] Write a runbook section for "gateway pool undersized" scenarios. (Unassigned – volunteers welcome)

No customer data was exposed. No billing impact. Apologies for the inconvenience.

Full timeline with timestamps is in the attached doc.

Thanks,
Derek
SRE Lead, enterprise.local

subject: Tip of the Week: Verifying Sender Addresses (30-Second Checklist)
body_text:
Hi all,

Short one this week. When an email asks you to do something unusual—transfer money, share a document, click a link—pause and check the sender's actual address, not just the display name.

30-second checklist:
1. Hover over (or tap) the sender name. Read the full domain.
2. Compare it to what you expect. "enterprise.local" ≠ "enterprise-lokal.com" ≠ "enterprise-local.net".
3. Check the Reply-To field separately. Attackers often match the From but hide the Reply-To.
4. If in doubt, call the person on a known number. Do NOT call the number in the email.

We publish an updated visual guide with side-by-side screenshots on our security docs site: https://docs.enterprise.local/security/phishing-guide

That page is updated every time we see a new variant, so it's worth bookmarking.

Stay safe,
Security Awareness

subject: [INC-2024-0402] Post-Mortem: DNS Resolution Failure (14 min)
body_text:
Ops team,

Post-mortem below for the April 2 DNS incident. No action items open beyond the two already in Jira. Full details attached as incident-0402-report.pdf.

Summary: Our secondary DNS node (dns-sec-02) lost upstream resolver connectivity for 14 minutes due to a BGP session flap on the uplink. Primary continued serving; TTLs on internal records were 300 s, so clients with fresh cache were unaffected. Clients with stale cache (TTL already expired) saw NXDOMAIN responses until the secondary recovered.

Impact: ~3% of API calls returned 502 between 09:41 and 09:55 UTC. No data loss. No PII exposure.

Preventive actions:
- [DONE] Upgraded the BGP hold-timer on the uplink switch from 90 s to 180 s. (Net-Ops, Apr 3)
- [OPEN] Add a synthetic DNS probe to the monitoring stack that alerts if internal resolution fails for > 60 s. (SRE, due Apr 20)

Let me know if you need the raw pcap or the resolver logs.

Regards,
Derek
SRE Lead, enterprise.local
INC-2024-0402

subject: Policy Update: Expanded Parental Leave – Effective January 1, 2026
body_html:
Expanded Parental Leave Policy

Effective January 1, 2026, Enterprise is updating its parental leave benefits as follows:

Birthing parent: 18 weeks of fully paid leave (up from 12).

Non-birthing / adoptive / foster parent: 12 weeks of fully paid leave (up from 8).

The leave period can be taken in a single block or split into two intervals, with each interval being a minimum of 4 consecutive weeks.

Employees must submit a leave request through the HR portal at least 30 days before the anticipated start date (6 weeks for unplanned circumstances). A manager sign-off is required, but cannot be denied for a valid medical or family reason.

Health benefits, 401(k) employer match, and accrued PTO continue uninterrupted during the leave period.

A dedicated Parental Leave Navigator (external counselor) will be available to help you plan re-entry, discuss part-time return options, and coordinate with your manager. Book a session via the HR portal under Resources → Parental Leave.

Questions? Contact hr-policy@enterprise.local or your People Business Partner.

Enterprise People & Culture

subject: Project Helios – Sprint 14 Wrap & Sprint 15 Kickoff
body_text:
Hi team,

Quick status on Helios before we kick off Sprint 15 tomorrow.

Sprint 14 finished 3 of 4 story points short. The auth-token refresh endpoint (JIRA HELIOS-412) is the main culprit. The fix is straightforward but we need to coordinate with the platform team on the JWT rotation policy.

Here's the retry logic I'm proposing for the token refresh handler:

```python
def refresh_token(current_token: str, max_retries: int = 3) -> str:
    for attempt in range(max_retries):
        resp = token_service.exchange(current_token)
        if resp.status == 200:
            return resp.new_token
        current_token = resp.retry_token
        time.sleep(0.5 * (2 ** attempt))
    raise TokenRefreshExhausted(f"Failed after {max_retries} attempts")
```

Sprint 15 focus:
- HELIOS-412: Token refresh (owner: me)
- HELIOS-430: Rate-limit middleware (owner: Priya)
- HELIOS-445: Dashboard v2 schema migration (owner: Tomás)

Risk flag: if the platform team doesn't confirm the rotation window by Thursday, HELIOS-412 slips to Sprint 16.

Let's sync at 10:00 tomorrow. Bring questions.

– Marcus

subject: BLOCKER: Project Lighthouse – Terraform state lock contention (OPS-2291)
body_text:
Folks,

Heads-up before standup. We're hitting a hard blocker on the Lighthouse infra-as-code pipeline.

Since ~14:00 yesterday the Terraform state backend (S3 + DynamoDB lock) has been throwing "Error acquiring the state lock" on roughly 40% of `terraform apply` runs in the staging environment. I've confirmed it's not a credential or IAM issue – the lock table shows orphaned entries from a failed CI runner that never released its lease.

What I've done so far:
- Purged 3 stale lock rows (IDs: lock-a7f2, lock-c910, lock-e33b)
- Restarted the two affected CI runners
- Temporarily bumped `retry_wait` in the backend config from 5s to 15s

What I need:
- @Devon: can you pull the DynamoDB stream logs for the last 24 h to see if there's a concurrent-write pattern I'm missing?
- @Sara: the Lighthouse Go/No-Go for the Thursday deploy is at risk if this isn't stable by tomorrow noon. Please brief the steering group.

Ticket: OPS-2291 (P1)
Severity: High – blocks all staging deploys for Lighthouse.

I'll keep updating the ticket. Ping me if you want to pair on the DynamoDB side.

Sofia

subject: Project Meridian – Revenue Recognition Risk Memo (Q3)
body_text:
Colleagues,

Per the request from the audit prep calendar, here is the risk memo for Meridian revenue recognition going into Q3 close.

Key risks and mitigations:

1. Multi-element performance obligations (PO-1147 series): We have 4 contracts where the implementation and licensing components are bundled. Under ASC 606 we need to allocate TSP. The current allocation model in the ERP assumes a 70/30 split; our legal team advises that 2 of those contracts may require a different split based on the standalone-selling-price evidence in the SOWs. Mitigation: I'm scheduling a working session with the contract owners next week to re-paper the allocation before the close.

2. Variable consideration (usage-based tier): The overage billing for the Platinum tier generated an 8% higher-than-modeled revenue in August. If the trend holds into September, the ceiling test in step 5 of the 5-step model will need a re-estimate. Mitigation: the revenue-analytics team is running a Monte Carlo on the trailing 6 months of usage; results due by the 22nd.

3. Contract modification accounting (Meridian-4402): A customer requested scope expansion mid-quarter. We've classified it as a separate contract, but I want a second opinion from external counsel before we book it. Expected cost: ~$4k in legal fees. Budget line: 5510-Professional Fees.

No items are expected to change the bottom line by more than 2% of Q3 revenue. I'll circulate the final memo with the close package.

Questions? Reply-all is fine.

Tomás

subject: Q3 Travel & Expense Policy – Updated Approval Thresholds and Lodging Caps
body_text:
Dear Sales Colleagues,

I am writing to communicate the updated Travel & Expense (T&E) policy that will govern all business travel bookings effective from 1 August 2025.

Summary of key changes:

1. Pre-approval thresholds:
   - Trips under 2 nights / under £400 total: self-approval via the T&E portal.
   - Trips of 2–5 nights or £400–£2,500: requires Team Lead sign-off.
   - Trips exceeding 5 nights or £2,500: requires Director-level approval.

2. Lodging caps (per night, including taxes):
   - London / New York / San Francisco: £350 (previously £300)
   - Other UK / EU cities: £220
   - All other destinations: £180
   - Suite upgrades are not reimbursable unless explicitly approved in writing by a VP.

3. Airfare:
   - Economy class is the standard. Premium economy requires a business justification attached to the booking request.
   - Bookings must be made via the corporate travel partner (Amex GBT portal) at least 14 calendar days in advance. Emergency bookings within 72 hours of departure require a written explanation.

4. Ground transport:
   - Taxis and ride-hailing services are capped at £60 per trip unless travelling from/to an airport where no rail alternative exists.
   - Rental cars: economy class, full-to-full fuel policy.

5. Meals & entertainment:
   - Per-diem for meals: £50/day (UK) or £65/day (international).
   - Client entertainment: no cap, but receipts and attendee list are mandatory. Alcohol beyond two drinks per person per event requires line-item justification.

6. Receipts:
   - All receipts over £25 must be submitted within 14 days of the expense date. Digital receipts (PDF or photo via the T&E mobile app) are acceptable.

The full policy document (T&E-2025-Q3) is available on the Intranet under Resources > Policies > Travel.

Please direct all questions to the Travel & Expense team (travel@enterprise.local) or your regional HR business partner.

Sincerely,

—
Jonathan Reeves
Head of Travel & Expense Policy
Corporate Services | Enterprise Local Corporation

subject: Code of Conduct – Annual Refresher & New AI Usage Guidelines
body_text:
Dear Team,

As part of our annual compliance cycle, I am pleased to share the updated Code of Conduct (CoC-2025) and, for the first time, a dedicated annex covering the acceptable use of generative AI tools in the course of work.

The CoC remains grounded in our four core values: Integrity, Accountability, Respect, and Stewardship. The 2025 revision adds:

Section 7 – Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence:
  7.1  Employees must not input customer PII, trade secrets, or confidential client data into any public-facing AI service.
  7.2  AI-generated content intended for external distribution (reports, marketing copy, code comments) must be reviewed and approved by a designated owner before release.
  7.3  Where AI tools are used for engineering work (e.g., code completion, test generation), the resulting artefacts must pass the standard peer-review and CI/CD pipeline without exception.
  7.4  Prohibited: using AI to fabricate credentials, bypass access controls, or generate misleading documentation.

Section 9 – Conflicts of Interest (unchanged in substance, clarified language on outside consulting and crypto-asset disclosures).

Section 12 – Whistleblowing: our reporting hotline remains confidential and available 24/7. Retaliation is a Category A disciplinary offence.

The full document is at /policies/CoC-2025.pdf.

Thank you for your continued commitment to doing the right thing.

Warm regards,

subject: Vault & Credential Management Policy Update – Rotation, Scoping, and Audit Logging (SEC-2025-112)
body_text:
Platform Team,

As a follow-up to last week's architecture review, I'm circulating the updated Vault & Credential Management policy that applies to all service accounts, CI/CD tokens, and secrets stored in our HashiCorp Vault cluster.

Summary of changes (ticket SEC-2025-112):

1. Rotation cadence:
   - Short-lived tokens (CI/CD, webhooks): max 1-hour TTL. No static long-lived tokens permitted for Tier-1 integrations.
   - Service account secrets: must be rotated every 30 days (previously 90). Automate via the rotation pipeline in the platform repo.
   - Human credentials (SSH keys, cloud console MFA): annual review remains, but any credential unused for 60 days is auto-revoked.

2. Scoping:
   - Each credential must be scoped to the minimum set of policies required. The catch-all "root" policy is now restricted to break-glass only and requires dual approval (two named individuals) to assume.
   - Vault paths must follow the convention: /enterprise/{service}/{env}/{purpose}. Example: /enterprise/payments/prod/nt-webhook-signing.

3. Audit logging:
   - All Vault reads, writes, and policy changes are logged to the SIEM (Splunk index: vault-audit). Retention: 2 years hot, 5 years cold.
   - Any anomalous access pattern (e.g., a service account reading outside its namespace) triggers an automatic alert to the SOC and suspends the token pending review.

4. Break-glass procedure:
   - Unchanged in principle, but the unseal key ceremony now requires three of five key-holders instead of two of five. Schedule is maintained by the on-call SRE rotation.

5. Deprecation window:
   - The legacy API tokens in the old token-store (pre-Vault migration) will be hard-revoked on 1 September 2025. Any service still using them will be unavailable. Please audit your integrations and migrate by 29 August.

I've attached the full policy PDF and the migration runbook. If your service uses the old token store, please confirm migration status to secops@enterprise.local by 22 August.

Regards,

—
Kofi Asante
Security Engineering Lead
Platform Security | Enterprise Local Corporation

subject: URGENT: Security Policy v4.2 Update – Effective Immediately
body_text:
All Staff,

This message serves as formal notification that Security Policy SP-2025-042 has been ratified by the Executive Risk Committee and is now in effect as of the close of business today.

Key changes in this revision include:

1. Mandatory multi-factor authentication (MFA) has been extended to all third-party SaaS integrations, including but not limited to CRM, project management, and document storage platforms. Previously, MFA was required only for internal systems and email access.

2. The acceptable use of personal devices (BYOD) for accessing enterprise data is now restricted to devices enrolled in the Mobile Device Management (MDM) platform. Devices that cannot be enrolled must be decommissioned from enterprise workflows within 30 calendar days.

3. Password rotation intervals for privileged accounts have been updated from 90 days to 180 days, aligned with NIST SP 800-63B guidance. However, any account flagged by the Identity Threat Detection system will still be subject to immediate credential reset regardless of the rotation schedule.

4. Data classification labels (Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted) must now be applied to all documents stored in the enterprise file share and cloud workspace. Unlabeled documents will be flagged by the DLP scanner and quarantined after a 14-day grace period.

The full policy document, including appendices A through F and the revised exception request workflow, is attached to this email as SP-2025-Q2.pdf. Please read the complete document rather than relying solely on this summary.

Questions regarding interpretation or applicability to your role should be directed to the Compliance Office at compliance@enterprise.local or via ticket in the ServiceNow portal (queue: Compliance-Policy).

Non-compliance with this policy may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment, in accordance with the Employee Handbook (Section 7.4).

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Regards,
Dr. Helena Voss
Director of Compliance & Risk
Enterprise Risk Management Office

subject: RE: [EXTERNAL] Data Retention Schedule – 2025 Revision
body_text:
Hi team,

Following up on last week's discussion in the Data Governance steering meeting, please find below the revised retention schedule for operational data categories. This supersedes the 2023 schedule (DRS-2023-011).

Please review the table below and confirm that your respective data stores align with the new retention windows by end of Q3.

Category | Retention Period | Disposal Method | Responsible Owner
---------|-----------------|-----------------|------------------
Customer PII | 7 years post-relationship | Certified shredding / cryptographic erase | Privacy Office
Transaction logs | 5 years | Secure overwrite (DoD 5220.22-M) | FinOps
HR records | 12 years post-employment | Certified destruction w/ certificate | HR Operations
Network telemetry | 90 days rolling | Automated purge (no manual step) | SecOps
Email archives | 7 years | Cryptographic erase | IT Infrastructure
Vendor contracts | 10 years post-expiry | Physical destruction (paper) / crypto-erase (digital) | Legal

A few important notes:

- The 90-day rolling window for network telemetry is non-negotiable per the DPA addendum with our primary hosting provider. Do not configure longer retention without written approval from Legal.

- For HR records, the 12-year clock begins at the date of final payroll processing, not the last day of employment. Please coordinate with the Payroll team if you need clarification on specific cases.

- The disposal method column specifies the minimum standard. You are free to use more secure methods, but the log entry must reference the specific standard applied.

If your current retention configuration does not match the table above, please file a ticket in the GRC portal under queue: Data-Retention-Migration and attach a brief impact assessment. The 30-day migration window closes on the last business day of the quarter.

Let me know if anything is unclear.

Best,
Marcus Webb
Senior Data Governance Analyst
Data Governance & Privacy Office

subject: Reminder: Password Policy Update Effective 1 Jul – Minimum Length & History
body_text:
Good morning all,

A quick reminder that the updated corporate password policy takes effect 1 July. The key changes, quoted from the v4.2 policy document approved by the InfoSec committee in March:

"Passwords must be a minimum of 14 characters. Users may not reuse any of their last 24 passwords. Passwords must not contain the company name, employee name, or common dictionary words."

- If your current password is under 14 characters, the next time you log in to Okta you will be prompted to rotate. You will have 14 days to comply.

subject: Phishing Awareness: The "Invoiced by Procurement" Lure – What to Look For
body_text:
We intercepted 47 targeted phishing attempts over the past 72 hours. The dominant template this week impersonates our Procurement team and uses the subject line "Overdue Invoice #INV-2024-08831 – Payment Hold".

Red flags in the samples we captured:

1. Sender domain is proseware-invoice.com, NOT proseware.com. One character of difference.
2. The attachment is a .zip containing a .js file disguised as an invoice PDF.
3. The "Urgent 4-hour deadline" language designed to suppress your natural caution.
4. The reply-to address points to a Gmail alias, not a proseware.com mailbox.

What to do if you received one:
- Do NOT open the attachment.
- Forward the raw email to phishing@enterprise.local (do not use "Reply").
- Delete it from your inbox.

If you already opened the attachment, disconnect from the network, contact IT immediately at ext. 4410, and do not power off the machine (forensics needs the RAM state).

Reported incidents this week: 12. Zero confirmed compromises. Good job, everyone.

Security Operations
enterprise.local

subject: RE: [Post-Mortem] SSO Outage 09 Jun 14:22–15:51 UTC – Root Cause & Actions
body_text:
Team,

Per the commitment made in the all-hands call yesterday, here is the condensed post-mortem for the Okta SSO outage that affected all internal and customer-facing apps for 89 minutes.

Reference: incident INC-2024-0609-03, ticket NET-4512.

Summary
14:22 UTC – A configuration push from the upstream identity provider (Okta) to our local SCIM sync agent introduced a malformed attribute mapping for the "department" claim. The sync agent began looping every 30 seconds, saturating the PostgreSQL replica.
14:47 UTC – Page fired to IT Operations. On-call (Priya) identified the sync loop via CPU saturation on db-replica-02.
15:12 UTC – Sync agent stopped; replica restarted. Token validation began recovering.
15:51 UTC – All services confirmed healthy. Cache TTLs expired and stale sessions flushed.

Root cause
A vendor-side schema change shipped without a compatibility window. Our sync agent (v2.3.1) did not handle the new nullable "department" field gracefully and entered a retry storm.

Corrective actions
1. Patch sync agent to v2.4.0 (handles nullable claims) – deployed 10 Jun. (Owner: M. Kowalski, due 10 Jun – DONE)
2. Add a circuit-breaker to the sync loop so it backs off after 5 failures in 30 s. (Owner: D. Ferreira, due 21 Jun)
3. Update the runbook for SSO outages to include a "stop-the-bleed" one-liner for the sync agent. (Owner: IT Ops, due 14 Jun)
4. Request a 7-day deprecation notice commitment from Okta in our enterprise SLA. (Owner: Procurement + Legal, due 30 Jun)

Impact
- Employee logins: 89 min degraded (fallback TOTP was available).
- Customer portal: 89 min, 0 data loss.
- CI/CD pipelines: ~40 build minutes lost; no code corruption.

Full timeline and metrics are in the Confluence page INC-2024-0609-03. Thank you for your patience.

Marta Kowalski
IT Operations
enterprise.local

subject: DNS CAA Record Update – Effective 18 Jun
body_text:
Hi Frontend,

We are adding Certificate Authority Authorization (CAA) records to the enterprise.local zone starting 18 Jun. This restricts which CAs are permitted to issue TLS certificates for our domains, as a defense against mis-issuance.

The new records (quoted from the change request DNS-2024-0037, approved in the 6 Jun platform board):

"0 issue "letsencrypt.org"; 0 issue "digicert.com"; 2 issuewild "";

What this means for you:
- The wildcard certificate for *.enterprise.local will need to be re-issued via DigiCert (or Let's Encrypt for non-wildcard). The current Let's Encrypt wildcard will simply stop renewing after 18 Jun.
- If you have any staging subdomains pointed at a self-signed cert in a local dev setup, those are unaffected – CAA only applies to publicly resolvable names.
- Our internal PKI (Proseware Vault enterprise CA) is not impacted because it is not a public CA.

No action is required from your team for production. For local dev, ignore the change.

If you spin up a new subdomain for a prototype, the IT Ops ticket queue will handle the CAA exception automatically.

Questions? #it-ops in Slack.

Regards,
D. Ferreira
IT Operations – DNS & PKI

subject: RE: Proseware Vault – Shared Credential Rotation Policy (from 4 Jun sync)
body_text:
Hi Data team,

Following up on the 4 Jun data-platform sync (Confluence page DATA-PLAT-042, action item #4):

Effective 1 July, all shared credentials stored in Proseware Vault must be rotated at least every 90 days. This replaces the current "rotate-on-compromise" model with a scheduled policy to reduce blast radius.

What changes:
- The Vault admin console will flag any shared secret older than 85 days with a yellow badge. At 90 days the secret is locked for non-admin access until rotated.
- Service-to-service tokens (e.g., the warehouse read-replica password, the ETL pipeline API token) are in scope. Application-specific secrets generated per-deployment are exempt.
- You will receive a calendar invite 7 days before the rotation window opens. The invite includes a step-by-step runbook for regenerating the credential in the target system and updating the Vault entry.

What does NOT change:
- Individual user passwords in the Vault are still governed by the 14-day Okta policy, not this 90-day rule.
- Read-only analytics tokens issued to the BI tool are exempt pending the Q3 token-v2 migration.

If your team has more than 12 shared secrets in Vault, Dario will schedule a 30-min working session with you to batch-rotate during the 1–5 Jul window so you are not doing it piecemeal. He will email you directly.

Thanks,
Marta Kowalski (IT Ops)
cc: D. Ferreira (SecOps)

  Expected: 200 OK

subject: [EXTERNAL] New issue #209 on wingtiptoys/api-gateway: "403 on /v2/orders with X-Forwarded-For header"
body_text:
A new issue was opened on wingtiptoys/api-gateway by external user @taylor-wingtip.

Issue #209 – 403 on /v2/orders with X-Forwarded-For header

Body:
  We're integrating our order-lookup flow with your v2 API. When we send the
  X-Forwarded-For header (standard for our CDN), the gateway returns
  403 Forbidden with body {"error":"invalid_origin"}.

  Reproduction:
    curl -H "X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.42" \
         -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
         https://api.wingtiptoys.com/v2/orders?limit=5

  Without the header the call succeeds (200). We suspect the origin-check
  middleware is treating the XFF value as the client IP and blocking it
  against the allow-list.

  Steps already tried:
   - Removed the header → 200 OK
   - Set XFF to our public egress (203.0.113.42) → 403
   - Set XFF to 10.0.0.1 → 403

  Is there a way to whitelist our egress range, or should we be using a
  different header? We need this resolved before our 06/20 launch.

Labels: bug, api-gateway, external-report
Milestone: v2.15.0

View issue: https://github.wingtiptoys.com/api-gateway/issues/209

– GitHub, via enterprise.local relay

subject: Updated Parental Leave Policy (effective Feb 1, 2025) – what changed
body_text:
Dear team,

After listening to your feedback over the past two quarters (thank you to the 214 of you who completed the People Pulse survey), we are rolling out a significantly updated Parental Leave Policy on February 1, 2025. Below is a plain-English summary of what changes and what stays the same.

WHAT'S NEW
- Duration: All eligible parents (birth, adoption, foster placement, or surrogacy) receive 18 weeks of paid leave, up from 12. The first 10 weeks are 100% of base salary; weeks 11–18 are 70%.
- Flexible start: You may begin leave up to 8 weeks before the expected due date or placement date, rather than only 4.
- Phased return: You have the option to take the 18 weeks in a single block OR split it into two segments (e.g., 12 weeks + 6 weeks) within a 12-month window, with a minimum 4-week gap between segments.
- Partner leave: Non-birthing partners receive the same 18 weeks. Previously this was 8 weeks. No documentation of a "primary caregiver" designation is required.
- Adoption & foster: The clock starts on the day the child enters your home, not the day of court finalization. This was one of the most common pieces of feedback.

WHAT STAYS THE SAME
- Eligibility: 12 months of continuous service (or equivalent for part-time). No change.
- Job protection: Full reinstatement to the same or an equivalent role. No change.
- Health benefits continuation: Coverage continues at the same premium level throughout leave. No change.
- FMLA interaction: The first 12 weeks still count toward your federal FMLA entitlement if you are covered. The additional 6 weeks are a company benefit and are not subject to FMLA rules.

WHAT STAYS THE SAME (cont'd)
- You do NOT need your partner's or your ex-partner's permission to take leave. The policy explicitly states that leave is an individual right.
- No medical documentation is required for the leave request itself. (You may need documentation for FMLA purposes; HR will walk you through that separately.)

HOW TO APPLY
1. Log in to Workday > My Profile > Time Off > Request Leave > Parental Leave.
2. Select the leave type, expected dates, and whether you want a single block or split.
3. Your manager is notified for scheduling only – they do NOT approve or deny the request.
4. HR Benefits confirms your premium continuation and updates your pay schedule.
5. You'll receive a written confirmation within 5 business days.

QUESTIONS?
- Policy owner: Priya Raman (priya.raman@enterprise.local)
- General HR: hr-helpdesk@enterprise.local, ext. 4410
- Legal review of the policy text: legal-ops@enterprise.local
- The full 14-page policy PDF is in Confluence: HR-Policies > Parental-Leave-2025

We know this is an area where people's lives are deeply personal. We want the policy to be clear, generous, and free of gatekeeping. If something in this email is still unclear, please reach out – that's the whole point of the feedback loop.

With gratitude,
Priya Raman

subject: Seattle HQ: New desk-sharing schedule starting Jan 6
body_html:
Hi everyone,

Following the feedback period in October (thank you to the 340 of you who submitted preferences), the Facilities team is implementing a revised desk-sharing and room-booking model at the Seattle HQ (1200 5th Ave) effective Monday, January 6, 2025.

What's changing:

  • Hot-desk zones (floors 2–4) will shift from a 2:1 person-to-desk ratio to a 1.4:1 ratio. You can reserve a specific desk in the RoomShare app up to 30 days out.
  • Dedicated desks (floors 5–7, lab benches, and the SRE war room) remain reserved for teams that require them. If your team was on a dedicated-desk allocation, no action is needed – your assignment carries over.
  • Meeting rooms: The minimum booking unit drops from 30 min to 15 min. Cancellation fee after 15 min of no-show is removed; instead, three no-shows in a rolling 30-day window will trigger a temporary 1-day booking hold. (See ticket FAC-2291 for the governance rationale.)
  • Focus pods (8 single-occupancy rooms, floors 3 and 5) remain first-come, first-served. No app reservation needed.

What's NOT changing:

  • Anchor-day expectation (Tuesday for most teams) – see the Remote Work Policy v3.2 thread.
  • Wellness room, lactation suite, and prayer/meditation room hours (24/7 with badge access).
  • Cafeteria, coffee bar, and bike-repair station hours.

The RoomShare app and web portal will be updated by Dec 30. If you have accessibility needs that require a specific location or setup, please contact facilities@enterprise.local before Jan 3 so we can arrange it ahead of the go-live.

Questions? Drop into the #facilities channel in Slack or stop by the front-desk kiosk on Mon–Fri, 9 AM–5 PM PT.

Thanks for your patience while we worked through the options. The 1.4:1 ratio was the compromise that got the most "thumbs up" in the survey – hopefully it feels like a workable middle ground. – Tom Okafor
Facilities & Workplace Experience
enterprise.local

subject: MANDATORY: Revised Information Security Policy v4.2 – Effective 1 July 2025
body_text:
Dear Colleagues,

Please be advised that the Board-approved Information Security Policy (ref: ISP-2025-0042) has been revised and will take effect on 1 July 2025. This update was driven by the Q1 audit findings (ticket SEC-AUDIT-2025-0117) and aligns our controls with NIST CSF 2.0.

Key changes include:
- Mandatory MFA for all remote access (no exceptions; see Appendix C for legacy system grandfathering through Q3).
- Prohibition of personal cloud storage for any data classified Internal or above.
- New incident reporting SLA: critical events must be escalated to the SOC within 15 minutes.
- Vendor risk assessments are now annual (previously biennial).

All managers are responsible for ensuring their direct reports complete the 45-minute refresher module on the LMS portal by 30 June. Non-completion will be flagged to department heads.

Questions may be directed to the Security Policy team at security-policy@enterprise.local or to the policy owner, Elena García, who leads the Governance & Risk function.

This communication constitutes formal notice. No separate acknowledgment form is required.

Regards,
Office of the CISO
Enterprise Security & Compliance Division

subject: Data Retention – New EU Customer Data Classification Matrix (DR-2025-012)

subject: Code of Conduct – New AI Usage Clause (Section 14.6): What It Means for You
body_text:
Dear Colleagues,

A quick, plain-English summary of the new Artificial Intelligence Usage clause (Section 14.6) in the 2025 Code of Conduct, which took effect 1 June:

WHAT IS ALLOWED
- Using approved corporate AI tools (listed in the IT Acceptable Use catalogue) for drafting, summarisation, brainstorming, and code-assist.
- Using personal AI tools for tasks that do not involve company data, customer data, or proprietary information.

WHAT IS NOT ALLOWED
- Pasting customer PII, financial model outputs, or unreleased product specs into any third-party AI service.
- Presenting AI-generated output as your own work in client deliverables without disclosure (the "transparency" rule).
- Using AI to generate code that will ship in production without a human review sign-off (pairs with our existing SDLC policy, SEC-DEV-019).

ENFORCEMENT
- Violations are handled under the standard disciplinary framework (Section 21). First offence: documented warning + mandatory retraining. Repeat or egregious: escalation to HR and Legal.
- The Compliance team will publish a short FAQ by end of June. Watch the intranet.

If you are unsure whether a specific use case is covered, ask your manager or email compliance@enterprise.local before you proceed. Better to check than to guess.

— Compliance & Ethics Office
Enterprise.local

subject: Introducing "Mindful Monday" – Our New Wellness Program
body_text:
Hi everyone,

Starting in three weeks, Enterprise is rolling out Mindful Monday, a weekly 20-minute guided mindfulness and movement session open to all employees. No experience necessary. No judgment. Just a quiet room, a mat (or your existing office chair), and a very calm voice on the speakerphone.

Sessions run every Monday, 8:00 AM, in Room 3-B (the one that smells faintly of lavender – that's intentional, not a facility issue).

Registration is optional. You can just walk in, or sign up via the Wellness tab in the intranet if you want a calendar invite.

Questions? wellness@enterprise.local or ping Priya in #mindful-monday on Slack.

Take care of yourselves out there.

– The HR & Wellness Team

subject: Parental Leave Policy Update – 2025 Revision
body_text:
All Employees,

The Executive Team has approved the 2025 revision to our Parental Leave Policy. The updated policy is effective January 1, 2025, and applies to all full-time and part-time (80+ hrs/week) employees. Key changes are summarized below; the full text is available at confluence.enterprise.local/policies/parental-leave-2025.

Summary of changes:
- Paid parental leave extended from 8 weeks to 12 weeks for all eligible employees (birth, adoption, foster placement, and surrogacy).
- The 12 weeks are now fully paid at 100% of base salary (previously 8 weeks at 100%, then 4 weeks at 60%).
- Partner leave (non-birthing parent) is now a minimum of 8 weeks at 100%, up from the previous 6 weeks at 80%.
- The policy now explicitly covers employees who become parents via egg/sperm donation, surrogacy, or gestational carrier arrangements, without requiring a specific relationship classification.
- The return-to-work transition period (ramp-up) of 2 weeks at 50% capacity is now guaranteed and cannot be waived by a manager.

From the HR Policy Committee statement:

  "We reviewed the 2022 policy against current industry benchmarks and our own retention data. The gap in paid leave duration was one of the top three factors cited in exit interviews for employees who left within their first 18 months. This update is a correction, not a perk."

  "We also heard clearly from employees that the previous language around 'eligible relationship' created confusion and, in some cases, made people feel they needed to justify their family structure to HR. The 2025 language removes that requirement entirely. If you are becoming a parent, you are covered. Full stop."

Implementation notes:
- Existing employees on leave under the 2022 policy will NOT be retroactively upgraded. This applies to leave starting on or after Jan 1, 2025.
- Managers: the People Ops team will run a 30-minute briefing for all people managers in November. You do not need to take action until then, but please forward this email to your direct reports.
- Questions: policy@enterprise.local or your assigned HR Business Partner.

Thank you for your attention to this. These policies exist to make sure that every employee can take the time they need without losing their place here.

– HR Policy & Compliance, enterprise.local

The Q4 wellness challenge is here, and yes, it's the step challenge again. You asked for it (or at least 347 people did, which we're choosing to call a mandate).

- Track your daily steps via the company health app (Apple Health, Google Fit, Fitbit, or the "I counted my steps on a napkin" method, which we technically accept if you submit a photo).

subject: Ticket NWT-4519 (SEV-1) – Resolution & Follow-up Summary
body_text:
Dear Mr. Chen,

We are writing to confirm that ticket NWT-4519 has been resolved.

Root cause: The 3.4.0 SDK introduced a change in the canonicalization of the X-Enterprise-Signature header construction. Specifically, the Date header is now appended AFTER the body digest rather than before, altering the HMAC input string. This was an undocumented behavioral change.

Resolution:
1. A corrected 3.4.1 SDK build is available at your portal download page (signed, checksum-verified).
2. The 3.3.x verification path will remain supported until 2025-07-30 (extended from the originally announced 2025-07-04).
3. We have updated the public changelog and webhook integration guide with the exact message-construction example.

Action items on our side (completed):
  – Changelog entry published (v3.4.1, 2025-06-20)
  – Webhook docs updated with worked signing example
  – 3.3.x deprecation window extended per above

We apologize for the disruption to your production webhook consumers and appreciate your patience.

Your support agent: Dara Patel (dara.patel@enterprise.local)
SLA compliance: Resolved in 6h 42m against a 4h SEV-1 target – SLA breached. A 15% credit will be applied to your next invoice per your contract §12.4.

If you require further assistance, please reply to this thread or reference NWT-4519 in a new ticket.

Sincerely,
Enterprise Platform Support

  • Webhook docs updated with worked signing example
  • 3.3.x deprecation window extended per above

subject: Update: Enterprise Credential Policy v3.2 – Effective Aug 1
body_text:
All Engineering,

I'm writing to announce the finalized v3.2 revision of our Enterprise Credential & Secret Management Policy. The full document is available in the internal wiki under /policies/credential-mgmt-v3.2. I'll summarize the key changes here, but please read the full text before August 1, when it becomes binding.

Section 4 – Rotation Cadence:
Effective August 1, all long-lived API keys (including OAuth client secrets, SaaS integration tokens, and internal service-account credentials) must be rotated no less frequently than every 90 days. The previous 180-day window is retired. Keys with a TTL shorter than 90 days (e.g., Vault-issued dynamic secrets) are exempt, as they are inherently ephemeral.

Section 7 – Storage & Transmission:
No credential of any kind may be stored in plaintext on developer laptops, in unencrypted cloud-storage buckets, or in source-code repositories (including private ones). The approved storage mechanism is HashiCorp Vault (enterprise tier) or the corporate password manager (1Password Business). If you are currently keeping a database password in a .env file that is checked into Git, you must migrate it to Vault by August 31. The DevOps team will provide a migration guide and office hours in the second week of July.

Section 11 – Incident Response:
If a credential is suspected to be compromised – whether through a public repo exposure, a social-engineering attempt, or a misconfigured S3 bucket – the first action must be immediate revocation in Vault or at the issuing service. Do not wait for Security Operations to confirm. Then file a P1 incident ticket and notify your manager. The 15-minute revocation SLA in Section 11.3 applies to all engineering staff, not just the on-call rotation.

Section 14 – Third-Party & Contractor Access:
Any contractor or external vendor who requires access to a production or staging credential must go through the Access Request Portal (ITSM ticket type: SEC_ACCESS_REQ). The credential must be scoped to the minimum necessary permissions and must expire no later than 7 days after the engagement ends. We will no longer accept email-based requests for credential sharing, even between trusted partners.

I know this is a lot to digest, and I appreciate that some of these changes will require you to rework existing pipelines or Terraform modules. The Platform Engineering team is standing up a dedicated help channel (#credential-policy-v32) in our Slack workspace starting Monday. Please use it for questions, migration help, or to flag edge cases I haven't anticipated.

If your team believes a specific requirement in v3.2 creates an operational conflict that cannot be resolved with the current tooling, please file a policy exception request by July 26. Exceptions are reviewed weekly by the CISO's office and are time-boxed to 30 days maximum.

Thank you for your attention to this. Safe credential practices are the single most effective thing we can do to reduce the blast radius of any future incident, and I want to make sure the policy supports you rather than getting in your way.

Best regards,

Dr. Helena Voss
Chief Technology Officer
enterprise.local

subject: RE: Credential storage for new Redis cluster (project_titan)
body_text:
Hi Infra,

Following up on Tuesday's standup action item. We're spinning up the new Redis cluster for project_titan next sprint and I need to sort out the credential story before we write the first Terraform module.

My proposed approach (hate to over-plan, but I've been burned by "we'll deal with auth later" before):

- Auth model: TLS mutual auth + ACL-based user scoping. No bare passwords in config files.
- Credential source: Vault, path /secret/project_titan/redis/. We'll use the dynamic-credentials engine so each pod gets a short-lived token (TTL 1h) rather than a shared long-lived password.
- Rotation: automatic via Vault's lease renewal; no manual rotation ticket needed unless the cert or ACL changes.
- Fallback: if the dynamic engine isn't stable enough for our workload yet, we fall back to a static secret in Vault with a 30-day TTL and an alert in PagerDuty 5 days before expiry. I'd prefer we don't need the fallback, but I want it documented so we're not scrambling at 2 a.m.

Can you confirm the Vault team has capacity to set up the dynamic-credentials mount by the start of sprint 24? And do we need to update the network policy to allow pod-to-Vault traffic on 8200/tcp, or is that already covered by the mesh mTLS policy?

Also, a small note: please do NOT put the initial admin password (yes, the one that's required to bootstrap the ACL before Vault takes over) into the runbook. We'll share it via the secure channel and it will be retired within 24 hours of cluster promotion. Standard procedure, just want to make sure nobody's got it in a Jira comment.

Thanks,
Ananya
